Title: Pulau Perhentian residents brace for Northeast Monsoon Floods
Article:
JERTIH: Residents in the village on Pulau Perhentian here have started making early preparations for the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), which is expected to bring heavy rain and pose a flood risk to low-lying areas of the village.
Resident Azizah Ab Rahman, 59, said the village was also vulnerable to flooding, especially when heavy rain coincided with high tides, causing water to stagnate and making it difficult for it to drain into the sea.
"In the past, during the MTL, this situation caused low-lying areas, such as Kampung Tengah, to be flooded up to a depth of almost one metre when rainwater flowing down from the hills could not drain into the sea due to the high tide.
"As a precaution, I began moving household items to higher ground a few days ago, as floods can occur at any time during the monsoon season," she told Bernama when met at her house on Pulau Perhentian yesterday.
Azizah, who has been living alone since her husband died several years ago, said her children worked and lived on the mainland, leaving her to seek help from neighbours to move heavy items, such as the refrigerator and washing machine, from the kitchen to the higher section of her house.
She said that although the flash floods usually receded within a few hours after the rain stopped, early preparations were important to prevent damage to household items and property losses.
Meanwhile, another resident, 36-year-old Hayatunnupus Nawawi said she had also placed her refrigerator in the living room on a specially built platform about 1.5 metres high to protect it from floodwaters.
"I have kept the refrigerator there permanently since last year's incident because it is difficult to move it when flooding occurs.
"I have two young children, aged five and nine, while my husband, Ali Abdullah, 36, is physically paralysed," she said.
Pulau Perhentian Village Development and Security Committee (JPKK) chairman Nik Zawawi Mohd Nor said about 30 houses were usually affected whenever flooding occurred in the village.
He said the floods were generally caused by heavy rain coinciding with high tides during the MTL, making it difficult for water to drain quickly into the sea.
"Flooding usually lasts about two hours and may occur several times throughout the MTL season, depending on rainfall and tidal conditions," he added. — BERNAMA

Title: Meghan on TV menu for 'Junior MasterChef Australia'
Article:
SYDNEY: Prince Harry's wife Meghan says she has agreed to feature as a special guest in television cooking sensation "Junior MasterChef Australia."
Meghan, who was a guest judge on "MasterChef Australia" this year, is to appear in next year's contest for young cooks on Network 10.
"When they approached me to come back and work with this young group of talent, it was an easy yes," the Duchess of Sussex said in a statement Tuesday.
"I love cooking with my own kids, so seeing what these young stars create in the kitchen is going to be a lot of fun."
The series is to be filmed in Melbourne next year, according to Australian broadcaster ABC.
Harry, the second son of King Charles III and estranged brother of heir to the throne Prince William, married Meghan, an American former actor, at Windsor Castle in May 2018.
The couple left Britain for the United States and quit royal duties in 2020, but made an unexpected return with their two children to live in the United Kingdom in August. — AFP

Title: Israel to give verdict on Netanyahu in pivotal election
Article:
JERUSALEM: A deeply divided Israel will head to the polls on Tuesday for the first time since Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack, with voters delivering their verdict on veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the country's rightward drift.
Israelis will cast their ballots in the shadow of three years of multi-front regional wars triggered by Oct 7, with the trauma still fresh and questions over accountability and security central to the campaign.
The close-fought vote comes as Israel looks increasingly isolated on the world stage, driven by a devastating military campaign in Gaza, soaring settlement construction and violence in the occupied West Bank, and a move towards hard-right religious nationalism.
The last polls to be published showed Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, running neck and neck with his main centrist rival Gadi Eisenkot, a political novice and former military chief whose mild manner is seen as the antithesis of the incumbent.
Some 7.3 million people are eligible to vote, with more than half a million young people due to cast their ballots for the first time. Surveys show they overwhelmingly identify as centre-right or right-wing.
Tens of thousands of Israelis are estimated to have flown in from abroad to vote in an election seen as crucial to deciding the future character of their country.
"I think this is one of the most important election days in the history of the state of Israel," Uriel Brandler, a 58-year-old real estate agent, told AFP in Jerusalem the day before the vote.
"The country definitely needs a change for the better in every aspect."
Netanyahu, 77, has served as Israel's prime minister on and off for more than 19 years.
The wily political operator focused heavily on his security credentials during his campaign, playing on his relationship with US President Donald Trump and insisting he is the only one who can keep Israelis safe.
In the years since Oct 7, Netanyahu led multiple wars that have seen Israeli forces reduce Gaza to rubble, occupy southern Lebanon and, for the first time, pummel arch-foe Iran with US help.
At home, Israelis have faced bombardment from Iran, Hamas, Lebanese militant group Hizbollah and Yemen's Houthi rebels.
'Not afraid to take action'
Zipporah Bennett, an 85-year-old retiree, said she was voting for Netanyahu "because he has had the experience of navigating the country through a lot of difficult seasons".
"He has the full support of the American government," she said, "and I believe he's a man who's not afraid to take action."
Netanyahu returned to power in December 2022, bringing into his coalition far-right ultra-nationalists who have since seen their political clout skyrocket.
The opposition has scorned the premier for his backing of ultra-Orthodox parties fighting to keep exemptions for religious Jewish students from being drafted into the military, which faces personnel shortages.
But one of the biggest criticisms levelled at Netanyahu is his failure to take responsibility for the Oct 7 attack, the deadliest day in the country's history.
Eisenkot, 66, has pledged to establish an independent state commission of inquiry into the security failures that led to the attack, something Netanyahu's government has resisted.
Seeking to unseat the premier is an informal bloc of parties led by Eisenkot's Yashar and spanning the right to the centre-left.
Eisenkot has vowed to prevent the creation of a Palestinian state and expressed support for Israeli settlements, but has promised to crack down on violent settlers.
Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu has publicly said they would partner with the predominantly Arab lists, which represent some 21 per cent of Israel's population and could become kingmakers if the results are as close as expected.
Final results could take days to trickle in, and it is highly unlikely that any single party will come close to the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member parliament.
Cobbling together a coalition could take weeks or months, with possible new elections on the horizon if negotiations fail.

Title: USTR Greer tells EU that loan to Airbus threatens trade truce on aircraft financing
Article:
WASHINGTON: US Trade Representative (USTR) Jamieson Greer told the European Union on Monday that a lack of information about its record-breaking loan to Airbus threatens a delicate transatlantic trade truce, including on financing large civil aircraft (LCA) projects.
In a statement, Greer expressed frustration that despite "ongoing requests," his office has received no details about the US$3.4 billion loan made in June from the European Investment Bank (EIB), the EU's official lending arm.
US planemaker Boeing had asked the US government in July to press for transparency on the loan, which came amid speculation that Airbus would use the funds to develop a new aircraft model.
"This situation injects substantial uncertainty into transatlantic trade in the aerospace sector," Greer said. "It is important this situation is resolved as soon as possible to ensure market-driven production in the aerospace sector and to avoid violation of the terms of our hard-won LCA deal."
An Airbus spokesman said the EIB loan "is a standard corporate financing facility, similar to commercially-available loans we've signed in the past.
"We are actively engaging with the relevant authorities and are happy to share more information about the loan with governments," the spokesman said in an emailed statement. The loan was also meant to diversify Airbus' funding sources, which was "necessary to manage the complexity of a high-value global production system and supply chain."
The US and EU fought a protracted 17-year battle over alleged aircraft subsidies at the World Trade Organisation (WTO), with both sides winning partial victories before agreeing to a five-year truce in 2021 that forestalled mutual tariffs on some US$11.5 billion worth of trade.
The truce was extended in July after the EU parliament approved a broader US trade deal that removed tariffs on US industrial goods in return for a 15 per cent US tariff on most EU goods. US President Donald Trump had threatened higher tariffs unless EU member states met a July 4 deadline for ratifying the deal initially reached in July 2025.
A key question for USTR is whether the terms of the EIB loan would be considered a subsidy for Airbus, as the WTO has found in the past on such loans.
Boeing did not immediately respond on Monday to requests for comment on Greer's statement.
The EIB said in July that it finances thousands of companies every year and denied offering Airbus any unusual support. "This is a normal loan, carrying interest, part of the EIB's overall financing activity," a spokesperson for the lender said.
Airbus chief financial officer Thomas Toepfer also told reporters in London in July that the loan had been taken out "completely at market level."

Title: Asian stocks surge as Anthropic IPO lifts sentiment ahead of earnings, central banks
Article:
SINGAPORE: Asian stocks surged on Tuesday as AI bellwether Anthropic's eagerly anticipated IPO filing lifted risk appetite ahead of tech earnings that will be a test for the AI trade, and central bank meetings that will influence near-term interest rates.
Claude-owner Anthropic disclosed steep loss and red-hot revenue growth in its filing for a US initial public offering, as investors increasingly dissect the potential payoff from massive AI spending and its profitability.
Also boosting sentiment was Meta Platforms' plans to raise up to US$95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising.
The currency markets are muted ahead of policy decisions from the Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan, with economists expecting all three to stand pat on interest rates, leaving the focus on comments from policymakers to gauge the rates outlook.
In stocks, tech-heavy South Korea's KOSPI gained more than four per cent in early trading while Japan's Nikkei was 1.9 per cent higher. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 1.2 per cent.
Nasdaq futures was up 0.4 per cent after US chip stocks rose 2.8 per cent in overnight trade, clocking its biggest one-day jump in a month. European stock futures dipped 0.23 per cent.
More than a third of S&P 500 companies are scheduled to report earnings this week, including hyperscalers Alphabet , Microsoft and Amazon.com.
"Given the increased AI scrutiny of late and circular arrangements, investors will want evidence that demand is broadening beyond these interconnected relationships to support the continued infrastructure expansion," said Anthony Saglimbene, Ameriprise's chief market strategist.
"Investors need confidence that aggressive capex spending reflects durable business needs and that profitability will hold up as new infrastructure comes into service," he said.
Brent crude futures eased 0.7 per cent to US$114.95 a barrel, drifting away from a six-month high as investors weighed the potential for a resolution in the US-Israeli war with Iran, keeping supply fears at bay though sentiment remained fragile.
Nick Twidale, chief market strategist at ATFX Global, said supply remains the key concern, and any developments that threaten physical exports could see Brent quickly retest recent highs and potentially push back towards US$120.
The nearly eight-month-old war has rippled across the Middle East, sending oil prices higher, stoking inflation worries and upending the global interest rates outlook, sharpening the focus on the central bank decisions this week.
Fed policymakers have telegraphed they will not raise short-term borrowing costs again this week, but with inflation concerns still front and centre, investors believe a rate-hike pause will not last for long. Traders are pricing in a hike from the Fed in December.
"Can we expect (US) growth to hold up in an environment of higher rates?," Geng Ngarmboonanant, head of macro and policy, multi-asset solutions, J.P. Morgan Asset Management, said.
"We think yes. We believe the US economy is going to be able to manage through higher interest rates."
The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note was steady at 4.992 per cent, staying below 5 per cent which it breached in September as investors scurried to Treasuries for safety during stock market tumult over AI worries.
The Japanese yen has been the haven of choice in currency markets and was last at 157.72 per dollar ahead of the BOJ decision on Friday.
The Japanese central bank is widely expected to declare victory in a nearly 14-year battle to hit its 2 per cent inflation target on Friday and emphasise the risk that prices could overshoot, signalling the chance of an interest rate hike as soon as December.
In commodities, gold eased a touch and was last at US$4,013.70 per ounce.

Title: Super El Nino: Ministry boosts food security measures
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Agriculture and Food Security Ministry has stepped up inter-agency preparedness to address the Super El Nino phenomenon, which is already showing early effects in the country.
Its minister, Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, said the agrofood sector faces mounting challenges from the Middle East conflict alongside extreme heat and prolonged dry weather, which could disrupt staple food supplies.
He said close monitoring is focused on dam water levels, particularly Kedah's Ahning Dam, where levels remain at alert and warning thresholds, threatening padi cultivation across the Muda granary area.
"The ministry has mobilised inter-agency preparedness measures through an integrated approach and the use of technology.
"These include implementing Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM), expanding the Smart Irrigation Monitoring System, introducing alternative water management methods for padi cultivation, and promoting Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) to ensure sustainable water security," he said when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 for the ministry in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
Mohamad said preparations were also under way in the fisheries sector, as rising sea temperatures shift fish distribution, affect aquaculture water quality, and threaten reef ecosystems.
He said capture fisheries and aquaculture production in affected areas could decline by 5,624 metric tonnes, or 1.5 per cent, this year.
To counter these challenges, Mohamad said the ministry had introduced early weather warning systems, the MyFSI location tracking system, and the Aquaculture Disaster Mitigation Plan, alongside the Fisheries Sector Climate Change Action Plan 2024-2030.
"Under the 2027 Budget, RM125.9 million in fiscal support has been allocated, including RM30 million for an additional 3,000 special small-boat licences, RM30 million for Agro BioFloc financing, RM10 million for Capture Fisheries Catalyst Financing, and RM2.3 million for biofisheries and biosecurity initiatives," he said.
He added that national frozen fish reserves are being built up, with total stocks reaching 10,000 metric tonnes as of Sept 30 to prepare for both Super El Nino and the Northeast Monsoon.
Overall, the ministry received an allocation of RM6.92 billion under Budget 2027, comprising RM4.85 billion for operating expenditure and RM2.07 billion for development expenditure.

Title: Study on National Disaster Management Bill to be completed within 12 months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A baseline study on the proposed Disaster Risk Reduction Act, following the proposal for the National Disaster Management Bill, is expected to be completed within 12 months.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the findings and recommendations of the study, conducted by the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), would be reviewed and coordinated with relevant ministries and agencies before the proposed policy and legislation are finalised.
"At present, a specific timeline for the tabling of the National Disaster Management Bill in the Dewan Rakyat has yet to be determined.
"This is because the current process still involves reviewing the need for, and the appropriate form of, the legislative framework," he said in a written reply published on the parliament website.
Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, was responding to a question from Zahir Hassan (PH-Wangsa Maju) regarding the latest developments in drafting the bill.
He said the findings would serve as an important basis for Nadma in determining efforts to strengthen disaster governance, particularly in prevention, risk reduction, and enhancing the resilience of communities and the nation.
"The government is taking an approach to ensure that the form and scope of the proposed legislation are truly suited to the country's disaster management needs, rather than simply enacting a new law without first identifying the actual gaps in the existing framework.
"This approach is also in line with the country's disaster management direction, which emphasises science-, data-, and technology-based preparedness, early action, early warning systems, clear command structures, and rapid and coordinated responses," he said.

Title: Gold eases as stronger dollar weighs, Fed meeting in focus
Article:
LONDON: Gold prices edged lower in early Asian trade on Tuesday as a firmer US dollar weighed on greenback-denominated bullion, while investors awaited Federal Reserve's policy meeting this week for clues on the interest-rate outlook.
FUNDAMENTALS
* Spot gold was down 0.1 per cent at $4,013.70 per ounce by 0045 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery dropped 0.3 per cent to $4,027.10.
* A firmer dollar reduces the appeal of dollar-priced bullion for overseas buyers.
* Federal Reserve policymakers have telegraphed they will not raise US short-term borrowing costs again this week, but with inflation concerns still front and center, investors believe a rate-hike pause will not last for long.
* Markets await the Fed's policy decision on Wednesday along with the Personal Consumption Expenditures data on Thursday, a key gauge closely watched by the central bank as it targets a two per cent inflation rate.
* Traders are pricing in about an 11 per cent chance of a rate hike this week and an 82 per cent chance of a December increase, according to the CME's FedWatch Tool.
* While gold is often seen as a hedge against inflation, higher interest rates tend to reduce the appeal of non-yielding bullion.
* On the geopolitical front, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said it intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles launched by Yemen's Houthis towards Saudi Arabia's Eastern Region early on Tuesday.
* Separately, top officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday in a bid to de-escalate the Middle East conflict.
* In other metals markets, Russia's Nornickel, the world's largest palladium producer, said a planned furnace overhaul could reduce output of key metals in 2027-2028.
* Spot silver edged 0.1 per cent higher to US$53.97 per ounce, platinum steadied at US$1,527.81 and palladium slid 0.7 per cent to US$1,042.43.

Title: TH traces funds to recover RM980m debt from Saudi firm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tabung Haji (TH) is tracing funds and bank transfers linked to Al-Rawda Investment for Real Estate Development and Project Management Ltd as part of efforts to recover outstanding debts.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said TH was pursuing recovery efforts with the relevant parties in Saudi Arabia.
He said agreements signed between TH and Al-Rawda from 2014 to 2017 involved legacy lease investments, under which TH leased four hotels in Makkah and Madinah on a long-term basis.
"TH has taken legal action and initiated enforcement proceedings in Saudi Arabian courts over a promissory note issued by Al-Rawda and guaranteed by its owner, following the company's prolonged failure to make payments under the agreement," he said in a written parliamentary reply yesterday.
Zulkifli said Al-Rawda initiated arbitration proceedings against TH in 2021, resulting in an award ordering the company to pay TH SAR899 million (RM980 million).
"TH and Al-Rawda signed a settlement agreement on Nov 27, 2024, setting out the terms for payment of the arbitration award.
"However, Al-Rawda paid only part of the amount, totalling SAR14.9 million (RM16.26 million).
"The company then failed to comply with the settlement agreement despite an extension granted by TH. The agreement was terminated on Jan 15, 2025," he said.
Zulkifli said TH had submitted a complaint to the Governor of Makkah in September 2025 over Al-Rawda's failure to fulfil its obligations.

Title: Crowds throng Kelantan gold shops as prices fall to RM503 a gramme
Article:
KOTA BARU: Gold prices falling to RM503 a gramme have drawn crowds to jewellery shops across Kelantan since yesterday.
A check around Pasar Siti Khadijah found many shops packed with customers eager to take advantage of the price drop, with gold selling for between RM503 and RM504 a gramme.
Customer Halima Osman, 45, said she was surprised by the sharp decline, as prices had previously approached RM600 a gramme.
"I love gold and have been watching prices fall over the past few weeks. I think RM503 is the lowest so far.
"Whenever prices drop, I take the opportunity to buy more for my collection.
"Today, I bought a bracelet because the price was low. We buy when prices are low and sell when they rise to make a profit," she said.
Another customer, Nur Ain Abdul Manaf, 30, bought a necklace and an anklet.
She said she had long viewed gold jewellery as a form of savings and investment.
"Now that prices are low, we buy. If we need money in the future, we can sell it. This seems to be the lowest price so far.
"When prices are low, we can add to our collection. While I was at the jewellery shop, everyone was there to buy, not sell," she said.

Title: Govt compiling refugee data through registration programme
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is collecting data on refugee communities nationwide through the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the first phase focused on those held at immigration depots.
He said the programme was expected to enter its second phase soon, covering holders of United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cards outside the depots.
"The purpose of this data collection is to enable the government to manage, coordinate and monitor the temporary presence of this group in the country before they are resettled in a third country or return to their countries of origin," he said in a written parliamentary reply yesterday.
Zahid was responding to Mohd Sany Hamzan (PH-Hulu Langat), who asked about the government's stance on international institutions operating in Malaysia, including UNHCR, which had allegedly failed to cooperate as expected and refused to share refugee data.
Zahid said international organisations provided an important platform for cooperation and expertise-sharing to address cross-border issues that countries could not tackle alone.
He said they also helped strengthen Malaysia's capacity and ease the burden of managing humanitarian issues.
"At present, the government also needs UNHCR to facilitate the resettlement of refugees in third countries, as those countries use UNHCR cards to verify refugees and confirm their status," he said.

Title: STR, Sara should remain short term to help with rising living costs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) assistance programmes must remain short-term measures rather than permanent features, as they are designed to help households cope with rising living costs and maintain their purchasing power, an economist said.
The more important objective should be to improve the economic status and living standards of recipients through education and healthcare, as well as cultivate a culture of self-improvement.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said continued reliance on such assistance could undermine the effectiveness of long-term government efforts in areas such as education, training, healthcare and infrastructure in promoting social mobility.
"This can be worrying as this could amplify the degree of income and wealth inequality, which can undermine social cohesion in the economy.
"So, the government should aspire that the recipient of cash aid would eventually be coming down as long-term policies on education, healthcare and infrastructure would be able to provide the right catalyst for the society to experience a better economic status," he told Bernama.
On the economic conditions needed to gradually phase out STR and Sara without putting vulnerable households at risk, Mohd Afzanizam said the government should monitor household income levels and ensure families continue to send their children to school and take care of their health.
"If there is any indication that their income level is rising, then I suppose the cash assistance can be gradually withdrawn.
"However, this can be quite challenging too as the family would have become so used to getting such assistance," he said.
He said government agencies should engage with communities to explain that the assistance is a temporary measure and encourage households to take advantage of government education and training programmes to improve their living standards.
"The main concern is one of moral hazard as the households become too dependent on the cash transfer programmes without enough effort to upgrade skills and earn a better living.
"The government needs to engage and communicate with Malaysian households that these are temporary measures," he added.
Meanwhile, CGS International Securities Malaysia chief economist Nazmi Idrus said STR and Sara should not be viewed as permanent forms of government support or unconditional handouts, but as measures to address income disparities and ensure that the poor have access to basic necessities.
"Assistance programmes help to balance out income disparity and create a more equal society. The government also has a responsibility to ensure that the basic needs of the poor are fulfilled. That is the purpose of STR & Sara. But cash handouts given unconditionally to everybody (like the RM100 Sara) are unnecessary," he said.
He said sustainable wage growth and higher household incomes were crucial to helping recipients eventually become financially independent, although achieving a living wage for everyone would take time.
"There is also risk that too much assistance eliminates the drive to work. So, it will be a balance between the need and the ability of the government to afford it," he said.
On the long-term economic and fiscal implications of making cash assistance a permanent feature of Malaysia's social protection system, Nazmi nevertheless said global trends suggest that such programmes were likely to remain in place.
"What this means is that the government may need to tax the rich more, to help the poor," he said.
He also suggested linking assistance to productivity-enhancing activities, such as requiring recipients of unemployment benefits to seek jobs or providing income support upon completion of training programmes.
"If we create a culture of self-improvement, then the people getting assistance may not be needing it permanently," he said.
Under the 2027 Budget, the government allocated RM16 billion for STR and Sara assistance programmes.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Landslide victim Dr Wong helped couple realise 12-year dream of parenthood
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The death of Dr Wong Kar Lin in a landslide has left a void in Penang's occupational safety and health (OSH) community and a profound personal loss for a family he helped fulfil its dream of parenthood.
The 73-year-old was killed when a
landslide
struck his home in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, on Sunday.
Dr Wong had served as an occupational health doctor (OHD) for decades, sharing his knowledge with OSH practitioners across Penang.
But to safety and health officer Azly Ahmad, 40, who had known him for 15 years, Dr Wong was more than a medical professional.
He helped turn Azly and his wife's 12-year wait for a child into reality.
Azly said he learnt in 2021 through a colleague that Dr Wong had a special interest in NaProTechnology, a natural fertility approach developed through the work of Dr Thomas W. Hilgers.
The approach focuses on understanding and monitoring a woman's reproductive cycle and offers an option for couples struggling to conceive.
"Alhamdulillah, with Allah's permission, our 12-year wait to welcome a child finally came to an end," Azly said in his tribute to Dr Wong.
He recalled that one particularly memorable moment was on Oct 5, 2022, when, during a conference, Dr Wong became the first person apart from Azly to learn that his wife was pregnant.
Azly said he was amazed by Dr Wong's ability to interpret his wife's Creighton Model FertilityCare System (CrMS) chart, adding that the doctor had even identified the baby's sex when the pregnancy was just two weeks along.
Beyond his professional expertise, Dr Wong became a father figure to the family and a grandfather to their child, Anaqy, Azly said.
"Although we were of different religions, he was like a father to my family and a grandfather to my child.
"Thank you, Allah, for bringing someone like him into our lives.
"You were such a kind person.
"Now, every time I look at my child, I will remember you and miss you. You will always be part of our story," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Oil eases on Middle East diplomacy hopes, Saudi attacks keep supply worries alive
Article:
LONDON: Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday as the potential for a resolution in the US-Israeli war on Iran kept supply fears at bay, but Brent stayed close to six-month highs as attacks on Saudi Arabia lowered hopes of immediate stability in the region.
Brent crude futures were down 66 cents, or 0.57 per cent, at US$115.15 a barrel as of 0000 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was down 44 cents, or 0.43 per cent, at US$101.32.
Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan held talks with Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday aimed at easing tensions in the Middle East. Saudi Arabia said the visit sought to establish open negotiating channels to "prevent the return of military escalation". The four countries agreed to continue talks with a view to strengthening cooperation in peace and security, Iranian state media reported.
Hopes of resolution in the conflict erased some fears of supply disruption, lowering risks and pressuring oil prices.
However, losses were limited as scope for peace looked fragile, with renewed attacksby Iran-aligned Houthis on key producer Saudi Arabia.
October has been the worst month for attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waterways, according to data compiled by a Washington-based think tank that has tracked maritime security incidents worldwide since 2017.
The war has rippled across the Middle East, placing the Strait of Hormuz at the center of the turmoil. The narrow waterway carried around a fifth of the world's energy supplies before the conflict erupted in February.
Last week, Brent prices surged to more than US$117 a barrel, the highest level since April, after a wave of Iranian attacks on tankers around the strait. Brent prices touched US$117 on Monday as well.
Elsewhere, Russian refiners are raising diesel production in October after the government granted export quotas following the Kremlin's supply agreement with the US, two industry sources close to the matter said.

Title: Explainer: Are Malaysian-linked firms in trouble over Singapore's haze notices?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Four companies with links to Malaysian-listed groups have been caught up in Singapore's efforts to tackle the haze that has lingered across the region for weeks.
But does receiving a notice mean they are responsible for the fires in Indonesia? And could they face penalties?
Here's what you need to know.
Which companies have Malaysian connections?
Two are Singapore-incorporated subsidiaries of Bursa Malaysia-listed TSH Resources Bhd – TSH Global Plantation Pte Ltd and TSH Oversea Pte Ltd.
The third is Wilmar International Ltd, a Singapore-listed agribusiness group in which Malaysia's PPB Group Bhd holds about 18.8 per cent.
The fourth, Kencana Agri Ltd, has a more indirect connection. Wilmar holds a 20 per cent stake in the company through a subsidiary.
What do the notices actually mean?
Singapore's National Environment Agency has asked 10 Singapore-registered companies to provide information about their Indonesian land concessions, corporate relationships and measures taken to prevent or control fires.
The notices are part of efforts to establish who may be responsible for the haze.
They do not mean the companies have been found responsible for causing pollution.
The notices differ from those issued to 10 Indonesian companies, which were ordered to take preventive measures against fires, including deploying firefighters, stopping burning activities and submitting prevention plans.
The Singapore-registered companies, meanwhile, have been asked to provide documents and information.
Put simply, one group has been told to tackle fires, while the other has been asked to help investigators establish responsibility.
Is Singapore using a new law?
No. The Transboundary Haze Pollution Act came into force in September 2014.
It allows Singapore to pursue companies over haze pollution affecting the country, even when the fires originate overseas.
What is significant in 2026 is the use of the existing law to seek information from Singapore-registered companies amid a prolonged haze episode linked to fires in Indonesia.
Could the Malaysian-linked companies face penalties?
Potentially, but not simply because they received notices.
Companies found responsible for haze pollution can face fines of up to S$2 million under the Act. Failure to comply with an information notice can also carry separate penalties.
For now, the companies must provide the requested information. TSH Resources' two subsidiaries have until Nov 2 to respond.
Whether further action follows will depend on what Singapore's investigators establish.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit opens higher against US dollar, major currencies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar and other major currencies on Tuesday as Malaysia's resilient economic fundamentals continued to support the local note amid lingering geopolitical risks in West Asia, an analyst said.
At 8am, the ringgit rose to 4.0840/0905 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0855/0895.

Title: Penang Muda wants hillside project approvals revoked
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang government must revoke all approvals for hillside development projects following a series of deadly landslides across the state.
Penang Muda state committee member Andika Putera said local councils, particularly the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) and Seberang Prai City Council (MBSP), must prioritise public safety and environmental sustainability over commercial interests.
He cited Sunday's incident in which 73-year-old Dr Wong Kar Lin was
killed
when a landslide caused part of his house in Lebuh Rambai 13, Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, to collapse.
Another landslide was reported in Tanjung Tokong on the same day.
"These recurring tragedies expose weaknesses in the control and approval of developments on sensitive hillslopes.
"Such projects only expose residents and workers to unnecessary risks," he said today.
Andika cited environmental governance expert Associate Professor Dr Haliza Abdul Rahman of Universiti Putra Malaysia, who said hillslopes were geotechnically and geomorphologically sensitive to physical disturbances and that recent incidents were linked to human activity.
In a Harian Metro report yesterday, she said slope cutting and hill-clearing without regular monitoring or adequate measures to maintain stability could disrupt the soil structure, reducing its cohesion and internal friction and making slopes unstable.
Andika also highlighted Penang's history of deadly hillside disasters in October, including the 2017 landslide at Lengkok Lembah Permai in Tanjung Bungah, which claimed 11 lives, and the 2018 Bukit Kukus paired road tragedy in Paya Terubong, which killed seven workers.
"People's lives cannot be sacrificed in the name of development.
"Firm and proactive measures must be taken now before more lives are lost due to the greed of those approving projects on hillslopes," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: Viral clip of distressed vendor sparks debate over trading permits
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A video showing a distressed woman amid the scattered aftermath of an alleged enforcement action has gone viral on social media, sparking widespread discussions online.
The video,
uploaded by TikTok user @mrmamahome,
captures the scene, with beverage containers, food items, and trading equipment strewn across the pavement.
In the footage, the vendor can be heard claiming that she has a licence, voicing her frustration, and alleging that she works hard to make an honest living.
She also confronts enforcement personnel, questioning the consistency of actions taken in the surrounding area.
The clip has since drawn mixed reactions across social media platforms.
Expressing sympathy over the situation, TikTok user @AzharBasri commented: "But why did they have to ruin all that food? Even if it was seized, I think it could have been loaded up properly."
On the other hand, others highlighted the procedural aspects of street trading. Commenting on the issue, TikTok user @bangcik pointed out: "Anyone can have a licence, but a permit to trade in that specific area is mandatory."
The New Straits Times (NST) has reached out to  Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) for a response regarding the incident.

Title: Democrats call for special counsel to probe Trump's Epstein ties
Article:
WASHINGTON: Democratic lawmakers called on Monday, eight days before crucial US midterm elections, for the appointment of a special counsel to probe President Donald Trump's ties to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
In a 53-page report, Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee revived allegations of sexual misconduct against Republican Trump, a one-time close friend of the disgraced financier.
Epstein died in federal custody in 2019 while awaiting trial on sex-trafficking charges involving minors, in what was determined to be a suicide.
Trump fought for months to prevent the Department of Justice (DOJ) from releasing the so-called "Epstein Files" but eventually signed a law passed by Congress requiring their publication.
The 80-year-old president's name appears repeatedly in the documents, but he denies any wrongdoing and has not been charged with any criminal offences connected to the affair.
Representative Jamie Raskin, the ranking Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, accused the Justice Department of covering up "crimes to protect the president".
"Five women have directly accused Trump of rape or sexual assault in Epstein's company or presence," Raskin said.
The House Judiciary Committee Democrats called on Attorney General Todd Blanche to appoint an independent special counsel to investigate Trump's ties to Epstein.
"At a minimum, DOJ and FBI's efforts to protect Trump rather than pursue justice require the appointment of an independent special counsel," they said.
"This special counsel should be tasked with investigating not only the President... but all of Epstein's potential accomplices and co-conspirators."
The House Democrats acknowledged, however, that the DOJ under Blanche, who is Trump's former personal attorney, was unlikely to "take even this minimal step".
"Determined to protect the President at any cost, DOJ itself now leads the cover-up of Epstein's sex trafficking operation," they said. "Todd Blanche has gone from being Donald Trump's personal attorney to his personal Attorney General."
White House Communications Director Steven Cheung denounced the report in a post on X, calling it "complete bullshit".
"This is what the media and Democrats do right before every election cycle – peddle lies and ridiculous accusations against the President for political gain," Cheung said.
"The American people see right through this garbage."
Ahead of the Nov 3 elections, which will decide control of Congress, Democrats have reportedly spent more than US$35 million on Epstein-related advertisements.
Epstein's former girlfriend, Ghislaine Maxwell, 64, is the only person who has been convicted of a crime in connection with Epstein and is serving a 20-year prison sentence for sex trafficking.
Maxwell was convicted in 2021 of supplying underage girls to Epstein, whose ties to powerful business executives, politicians, celebrities and academics have fuelled years of scrutiny and conspiracy theories.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Only Samalaju records unhealthy air quality this morning
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Samalaju, Sarawak was the only area in the country to record an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading as of 7am today.
According to the Department of Environment's (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Samalaju recorded an API reading of 151.
Another 42 areas recorded moderate API readings, including Bintulu, Serian, Sibu, Batu Muda, Kluang and Kuching.
Meanwhile, 25 stations recorded good API readings, including Port Dickson, Limbang, Bandaraya Melaka, Tanah Merah and Kemaman.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are hazardous.

Title: RM1.65mil durian orchard scam: CEO to be charged today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A chief executive officer of a fruit and vegetable wholesale, import, and export company is expected to be charged in court today over a durian orchard purchase scam involving about RM1.65 million.
The suspect, in his 50s, was arrested after giving a statement at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) headquarters in Putrajaya at 12pm yesterday.
A source said initial investigations revealed the suspect committed the offence in February 2024, but the purchase of the orchard never materialised.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrest.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code and the suspect will be charged at the Shah Alam Court in Selangor this morning.
It was previously reported that the MACC launched Op Kingfruit over a durian investment scam in Raub, Pahang, freezing bank accounts and seizing assets worth RM16.15 million.

Title: Johor Gleneagles Hospital expands university partnerships to nurture future nurses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Johor Gleneagles Hospital plans to expand its partnerships with universities and educational institutions to offer more sponsorship opportunities to students pursuing nursing careers.
It said the initiative builds on the hospital's existing collaborations with Nilai University and Universiti Selangor (Unisel) under its Nursing Sponsorship Programme.
"Selected students receive support covering tuition fees, monthly allowances and medical benefits throughout their studies. The programme also provides a pathway to employment at the hospital after graduation," it said in a statement.
Since its introduction in 2022, the programme has supported 248 students. Of these, 51 have graduated, with 17 already joining Johor Gleneagles Hospital.
The remaining 34 graduates, who completed their studies in 2026, are expected to join the hospital. Another 197 sponsored students are currently pursuing their nursing education.
Johor Gleneagles Hospital chief operating officer Thanabalan Muthaliar said investing in aspiring nurses early was essential to developing the future nursing workforce.
"Developing the nursing workforce of the future requires us to invest in talent early. By working with educational institutions, we can support students during their training and help prepare them for the realities of patient care.
"We want to build on what we have established with our existing university partners and work with more institutions to create opportunities for aspiring nurses," he said.
Beyond financial sponsorship, the hospital offers nurses exposure to specialised areas of care, opportunities to strengthen their clinical skills and access to continuous professional development throughout their careers.
The education-to-employment approach forms part of the hospital's long-term efforts to develop Malaysian nursing talent and strengthen the healthcare workforce.
As part of IHH Healthcare Malaysia's network of 18 hospitals nationwide, Johor Gleneagles Hospital also contributes to the group's broader efforts to develop healthcare professionals who can meet the changing needs of patients and communities across Malaysia.

Title: Britain will not join Canada-led defence bank initiative
Article:
BENGALURU: Britain will not join the Canada-led Defence, Security and Resilience Bank, in a setback to efforts to create the world's first global defence bank, according to a person familiar with the matter.
The two countries instead said on Sunday that they would develop a framework for cooperation between their respective defence-funding initiatives, establishing two distinct but complementary institutions to support each other on investment opportunities and strategic challenges.
"We have been working closely to consider how the Multilateral Defence Mechanism (MDM) and Defence, Security and Resilience Bank (DSRB) can best advance our shared objectives," the statement said.
The two governments were unable to agree on key issues, including the location of the headquarters of a joint institution, the level of joint procurement, lending to members and the rules governing new members, a second person said.
The MDM will focus on accelerating defence investment, joint procurement through financing and bringing together demand across Nato allies to reduce procurement costs, while the DSRB will complement it by supporting investment in defence industries and supply chains, with a greater focus on lending to individual sovereign states, the person added.
The DSRB, which will be based in Canada, has faced challenges securing support from larger European nations. Reuters was first to report in September last year that Britain had declined to join the project.
There were hopes that Britain would reconsider its position under new Prime Minister Andy Burnham and his team. Germany had previously declined to join. A spokesperson for the German Finance Ministry said Germany was an observer in the negotiations on the DSRB's charter and was reviewing outstanding questions.
Britain and Canada said the MDM and DSRB would be designed to work in close partnership so they could support each other on emerging industrial priorities, investment opportunities and strategic financing challenges.
Aiming to raise billions
The DSRB has been aiming to raise around €100 billion (US$112 billion) and use the money to lend at low cost to governments and contractors for defence projects. It will also offer guarantees to lenders financing smaller firms considered riskier borrowers.
So far, Albania, Belgium, Greece, Latvia, Luxembourg, Romania, Turkiye and Ukraine have pledged their support, along with Canada.
Canadian Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne said the group would meet in Luxembourg on November 30 to sign articles of agreement establishing the bank.
"Membership (is) open to other allies and close partners who share the Bank's objective," he said in a statement.
Reuters previously reported that potential members had not joined because of concerns including whether the DSRB could offer cheaper financing than highly rated national governments, as well as the amount of capital countries would need to commit, the bank's governance and overlaps with existing initiatives.
Britain's Defence Secretary Wes Streeting had recently described the DSRB as a "really interesting and innovative mechanism" and said he did not see the proposed defence bank and MDM as being in competition.
Britain previously declined to join, citing concerns over value for money. Reuters previously reported that Burnham discussed the DSRB alongside the MDM initiative with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in July and with Luxembourg Prime Minister Luc Frieden during an August visit to Kyiv.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bangladesh courts Malaysian tourists with tourism push
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bangladesh is seeking to attract more Malaysian tourists by leveraging shared cultural traditions, religious values and culinary preferences between the two countries.
Bangladesh High Commissioner to Malaysia Manjurul Karim Khan Chowdhury said stronger cooperation between the tourism industries could boost tourist arrivals and people-to-people exchanges.
He said this at the Bangladesh Tourism Presentation at Wyndham Kuala Lumpur yesterday, which showcased the country's attractions, heritage and tourism infrastructure to Malaysian industry players.
The event was organised by Travel Canvas with the support of the Bangladesh High Commission, Bangladesh Tourism Board (BTB) and Bangladesh-Malaysia Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BMCCI).
"Bangladesh's scenic landscapes, historical and archaeological sites, cultural diversity, cuisine and hospitality, as well as its tourism infrastructure and growth potential, are something all Malaysians must explore at least once.
"Similarities in religious traditions, cultural values and food preferences make Bangladesh an attractive destination for Malaysian travellers and provide opportunities to develop tailored tourism packages," he said in his welcome speech.
Representatives from the Bumiputra Travel and Tour Agents Association (BTTA), Malaysian Chinese Tourism Association (MCTA) and Malaysian Indian Tour and Travel Association (MITTA) attended the event.
An interactive session involving the associations, travel agents and tour operators from both countries was also held to explore joint initiatives and expand tourism packages to encourage more travel between Bangladesh and Malaysia.
Khan Chowdhury also unveiled Travel Canvas's publication, Bangladesh – The World's Largest Delta: An Untold Story.
The book provides historical information and highlights tourist attractions to explore when visiting Bangladesh.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Brazil's defeated presidential candidate says court barred him from leaving country
Article:
WASHINGTON: Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro said on Monday that the Supreme Court had ordered him to surrender his passports and barred him from leaving the country following his loss to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Sunday's run-off election, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
In a video posted on X, the senator said Federal Police officers had served him with the order after he visited his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest.
Bolsonaro said Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes had issued the ruling on Sunday night, shortly after Lula was declared the winner.
A copy of the court order was not immediately available, and the legal grounds for the travel restriction remained unclear.
Bolsonaro said the decision was based on a statement made on Oct 23 by his brother, Eduardo Bolsonaro, suggesting that he should leave Brazil if he lost the election.
"I never thought about leaving the country," Bolsonaro said, adding that he would comply with the passport surrender order while challenging the ruling.
He described the decision as an attempt to intimidate him and vowed to continue his political activities.
Bolsonaro also reiterated plans to seek the disqualification of Lula's winning ticket, alleging irregularities in Sunday's vote. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tighter economics on Cress, but still viable
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The new System Access Charge (SAC) under the Acceleration Package of the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (Cress) announced by the Energy and Water Transformation Ministry comes as a surprise to renewable energy developers (RED) and green consumers (GCs).
The introduction of the four sen per kWh in the system for GCs is the issue at hand.
A director of an RE developer pointed out that GCs are reluctant to accept the charge, as it can be increased every regulatory period (RP) by the authority.
"GCs do not want to face the possibility of the SAC being revised upwards every RP. They are asking REDs to bear this cost, and just charge them with a fixed tariff over a 10 or 20 year period," said the director with whom Business Times spoke to.
The director claimed that the Cress Acceleration Package might see low demand, due to the reluctance of the GCs to accept the SAC imposed on them. At the same time, the package is only for renewable energy plants that are completed before Dec 31, 2028.
Cypark Resources Bhd chief investment officer Belqaizi Taufik said that under the current Cress Acceleration Package, the economics are tighter than what the industry initially expected when 14 sen/kWh SAC was announced on Sept 18.
However, the commercial case remains and Cress can still be competitive for large energy users, particularly data centres, said Belqaizi in a written response to Business Times' questions.
This is because the combined SAC of 18 sen/kWh remains below the previous 20 sen/kWh structure, and the 14 sen/kWh charge is fixed for 10 years, giving cost certainty for the REDs and their clients.
"For Cypark, we remain positive. We are actively pursuing opportunities within the growing data centre ecosystem, including renewable energy supply and the supporting energy infrastructure required by these developments," said Belqaizi.
On Sept 18, Petra announced that the government has agreed to implement the acceleration package of Cress with a SAC of 14 sen/kWh for firm supply. In addition, a 10-year contractual period between the RED and GC will be enforced.
Following the announcement, share prices of REDs such as Solarvest Holdings Bhd, Samaiden Group Bhd, Northern Solar Holdings Bhd, Pekat Group Bhd and Cypark rallied as the market bet on them benefitting from the Cress acceleration package.
Share price of Solarvest surged 35 per cent within just about one week, from RM3.33 closing price on Sept 18 to a high of RM4.49 on Sept 29.
Pekat's share price ran from RM2.11 to RM2.98 – an increase of 41 per cent – during the period.
Northern Solar saw its share price surged 87 per cent during the period to RM1.29, while Samaiden rallied 63 per cent to close at RM3.18 on Sept 29, from RM1.95 on Sept 18.
Cypark saw a milder jump during the period, but was still up by 22.7 per cent to 54 sen on Sept 29.
However, the details of the acceleration package that was revealed by the EC in a briefing on Oct 13  where it introduced the four sen/kWh SAC on GC, brought uncertainty to the bankability of Cress.
As a result, investors' dumped REDs' shares. Pekat saw its share price plunge 13 per cent in two days between Oct 13 and 15, to close at RM2.53, while Samaiden saw a 9.8 per cent plunge in its share price during the period.
Solarvest and Northern Solar also declined during the two-day period, but at a milder quantum.
Cypark bucked the trend, with its share price jumped 34 per cent to 71 sen as of Oct 15, before plunging to 65 sen on Oct 20.
Can the commercial arrangement between the REDs and GCs be restructured around the 4 sen/kWh SAC?
For Cypark's Belqaizi, yes they can.
"For the GC, the key consideration is whether the total cost remains competitive against its alternative electricity supply. For the RED, the project still needs to provide an appropriate return and remain bankable.
"There may therefore be room to share or price that cost through the overall tariff, depending on the economics and structure of each project," he said.
Pekat CEO Tai Yee Chee also thinks that the Cress Acceleration Package is still bankable, as the effective SAC has come down 28 per cent, from 25 sen/kWh at inception to 18 sen.
The 14 sen/kWh developer component that is fixed for 10 years is what lenders need to underwrite project debt, he said.
"At an all-in cost of around 48 to 53 sen/kWh, Cress remains competitive against the mid-50s sen/kWh data centres currently paying Tenaga Nasional Bhd before the automatic fuel adjustment.
"The scheme is viable — what the market now needs is for the supplementary guidelines to land on time so negotiations can close," said Tai in a written response to Business Times' questions.
However, will RED be required to absorb all the SACs, including the variable portion that is imposed in GCs, in order to secure a Cress contract?
While the GC's desire for cost certainty is understandable – data centres make 20-year investment commitments – fixing the 4 sen/kWh SAC is a regulatory decision, not one that REDs can offer to absorb, said Tai.
"Grid costs evolve, and the regulator needs the ability to adjust for genuine changes," he said.
Tai added that a more practical outcome would be a transparent review mechanism with defined principles and caps on escalation, so that both GCs and REDs can plan with confidence even if the rate adjusts.
"The four sen is a small component of the total bill – even if it moves by one or two sen per RP, the impact is manageable relative to the savings Cress delivers against conventional tariffs," he said.
For Belqaizi of Cypark, there is merit in providing longer-term certainty on the SAC, particularly for data centres and other large energy users that are making long-term investment and renewable energy commitments.
"Having greater visibility over the SAC for a period that is better aligned with the tenure of these contracts would make it easier for GCs to commit, while also giving REDs and financiers greater certainty when assessing project economics and bankability," he said.
He added that greater long-term certainty would be positive for the overall Cress ecosystem, by helping accelerate contracting and investment, bringing more renewable energy capacity onto the grid and supporting Malaysia's ability to attract large investments that require green energy.
"The current framework is already a positive step in that direction. Any further measures that provide greater long-term cost visibility would, in our view, strengthen Cress and support its wider adoption," said Belqaizi.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MGS could face renewed volatility as US Fed look at rates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields and foreign fund flows could face renewed volatility following this week's US Federal Reserve meeting, as investors assess the implications of its policy outlook for global bond markets.
Economist Professor Geoffrey Williams said a US rate increase could put some upward pressure on MGS yields, although the impact would likely be limited because Malaysian government bonds were predominantly held by domestic investors.
He added that the move could also weaken the ringgit, although he viewed some depreciation as potentially necessary.
Trade View analyst Neoh Jia Man also expects the Fed to maintain interest rates, citing elevated energy costs linked to Middle East tensions and signs of a cooling US labour market.
"The Fed may see this as temporary. At the same time, the labour market is cooling, especially in hiring. Having hiked only last month, we think the Fed will wait for more data," he said.
Neoh said the 10-year MGS yield had fallen by more than 20 basis points from its mid-September peak, suggesting the market had largely priced in a Fed rate hold.
However, he warned that a surprise rate hike or a more hawkish policy outlook could push up short-term MGS yields and accelerate foreign fund outflows.
Equities could also face pressure from such outflows, although Neoh said valuations in certain sectors had become attractive and remained supported by strong fundamentals.
With a rate hold widely expected, Innes said Malaysian markets would likely take their direction less from the actual decision and more from movements in US Treasury yields.
"If those concerns drive US Treasury yields lower, MGS could benefit from improved relative value and renewed foreign interest," he said.
However, he cautioned that the benefits could be offset if falling yields reflected deeper concerns about an unwinding of AI investment, potentially triggering broader risk aversion and weakening foreign equity flows.
RAM Ratings, in its Mid-Week Bond Market Update dated Oct 22, identified the Oct 27-28 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting as a key external catalyst for Malaysia's bond market.
The rating agency warned that changes in US monetary policy guidance could trigger a repricing of US Treasury yields, spilling over into MGS, particularly longer-dated securities.
The 10-year MGS yield edged up to 3.92 per cent on Oct 21 from 3.90 per cent a week earlier, while the corresponding US Treasury yield fell to 5.13 per cent from 5.19 per cent.
The yield differential between the two benchmarks narrowed to negative 120.6 basis points on Oct 21 from negative 128.8 basis points on Oct 14, modestly improving the relative yield appeal of Malaysian government bonds.
However, foreign investors recorded a net outflow of RM570 million from Malaysian government bonds in the week ended Oct 14, despite overall foreign bond holdings registering a marginal net inflow of RM30 million.
The overall inflow was supported by RM610 million in corporate bond purchases, which offset the outflow from government bonds.
RAM Ratings said Malaysia's headline inflation eased to 1.8 per cent in September from 1.9 per cent in August, reducing the urgency for a policy rate hike.
"Attention now shifts to the Nov 5 Monetary Policy Committee meeting, with Bank Negara's assessment of inflation and domestic demand strength relevant for short-end MGS pricing," it said.
Williams expects a modest increase in US interest rates, citing strong demand and the risk of inflationary pressure.
"I expect a small increase in US interest rates because there is strong demand and their conventional approach will be to raise rates in anticipation of inflation," he said.
SPI Asset Management managing director Stephen Innes, however, expects the Fed to maintain interest rates at its upcoming meeting, saying financial conditions have already tightened amid pressure on equities and waning enthusiasm for artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks.
"Inflation remains uncomfortable, particularly with oil prices elevated, but financial conditions have already tightened considerably as equities have come under pressure and the AI trade begins to lose some of its shine," he said.
Innes said the sustainability of AI investment spending had become an increasingly important consideration for bond investors, given the substantial financing requirements behind the boom.
He said a slowdown in AI capital expenditure could weigh on US economic growth, reducing the need for further monetary tightening.
"For now, patience is the sensible option. The Fed can afford to sit on its hands and see whether inflation or weakening growth wins this particular tug of war," he said.
Bank Negara expected to maintain policy rate
On domestic monetary policy, Williams expects Bank Negara to keep its policy rate unchanged, using other measures to manage financial markets if needed.
Neoh said a Fed rate hike or a more hawkish stance would increase the possibility of Bank Negara raising rates, although he expected such a move to be more likely next year than this year.
"Inflation is still benign, consumer sentiment is weakening, and the ringgit is stable against the US dollar. Hence, we expect Bank Negara to keep the overnight policy rate unchanged unless domestic data change substantially," he said.
Innes also expects Bank Negara to remain patient, citing resilient domestic growth and relatively contained inflation.
"For Bank Negara, the sensible approach is to remain patient. Domestic growth has been resilient and inflation relatively contained, so there is little urgency to move the policy rate in either direction," he said.
He added that the Fed would remain an important policy reference for central banks, including Bank Negara, as they navigate persistent inflationary pressures alongside risks to global growth.
"I think the Fed will remain the main policy anchor for many central banks, including Bank Negara, as they navigate this increasingly narrow passage between inflation and slowing global growth," he said.
Innes added that elevated oil prices continued to pose inflationary risks, while a potential slowdown in AI investment could weaken demand and employment, complicating the outlook for central banks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump offers US$1mil reward for voter fraud reports ahead of midterm elections
Article:
WASHNIGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that he plans to pay US$1 million (RM4.09 million) to anyone reporting voter fraud in past elections or the upcoming midterm elections on Nov 3, provided the information leads to the arrest and conviction of those responsible, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
"Anybody reporting Voter Fraud in the past Elections, or the upcoming 2026 Midterm Election, will be paid US$1,000,000 upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud!" Trump said on Truth Social.
The announcement comes as the US prepares to hold midterm elections next week, with voters set to decide which party controls Congress amid heightened political disputes over election integrity. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Denying spouse money may constitute domestic violence, says Nancy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Being denied money for clothing, reprimanded over online purchases or forced to rely entirely on a partner for personal needs are among the situations that may constitute economic abuse within a household.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said domestic violence extended beyond physical and emotional abuse to include economic control, which could affect a victim's well-being and self-confidence.
She said this form of abuse warranted attention as it could occur in everyday situations, such as when a partner failed to provide money for basic family necessities or controlled personal spending, leaving the victim without financial autonomy.
"For example, a husband returns home expecting his wife to prepare a meal. If she is not working and has no money of her own, and he fails to provide funds for household necessities, how is she supposed to cook?
"Another example is when a wife wants to buy clothes but does not have the means to do so, leaving her unable to shop like other women. If she orders items online, she may end up being scolded by her husband. This is a common occurrence and has become a new challenge in life today," she said during an appearance on Bernama TV's Ruang Bicara programme here last night.
Nancy said such financial control could strip victims of the freedom to make decisions about their own needs, particularly if they had no income or access to funds.
According to her, police statistics showed an increase in domestic violence cases, from 5,507 in 2023 to 7,016 in 2024 and 7,391 in 2025, with 5,278 cases recorded from January to August this year.
"Domestic violence can take various forms and occur in different situations, but the challenge arises when victims choose to remain silent and do not seek help. In some cases, even after lodging a report, they later withdraw it out of fear," she said.
In this regard, Nancy said the ministry provided various forms of support to help victims escape abusive situations and rebuild their lives, including counselling services, intervention measures and financial assistance to attend court proceedings if necessary.
She stressed that addressing domestic violence was also vital to protect children who witnessed abuse at home, as such experiences could influence how they viewed family relationships as they grew older.
"We do not want children who witness such behaviour to grow up and repeat it because they have come to view it as normal," she said.
Nancy therefore urged the public not to treat domestic violence as merely a private family matter, but to report any known or suspected incidents by calling Talian Kasih at 15999 or sending a WhatsApp message to 019-2615999.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Syria says at least six dead in Jordan strikes
Article:
DAMASCUS: Syrian authorities said at least six people were killed in strikes on Monday in the country's south, as Jordan said it had targeted "terrorist organisations" after a deadly jihadist attack on a church.
In an updated statement, health authorities in Daraa province reported "six martyrs, including three children and a woman", after earlier reporting eight victims.
Syria's civil defence agency instead reported a total of seven people killed in several locations — six of them in Daraa province, including three children.
It also reported that a man was killed when a strike targeted a home in neighbouring Sweida province, adding that his body was still being recovered from under the rubble.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid urges public to stay alert as northeast monsoon begins today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has urged the public to stay vigilant and prioritise safety as the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon is expected to begin today.
He said the monsoon, expected to persist until March 2027, could bring prolonged heavy rainfall, flooding and rough seas, threatening residents’ safety, particularly in vulnerable areas.
He said the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecasts indicated that three to five episodes of prolonged heavy rainfall could occur between November 2026 and January 2027.
“This could increase the risk of flooding, particularly in areas near rivers and low-lying areas,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Ahmad Zahid said strong winds during the period could also cause rough seas and rising sea levels in the South China Sea.
He advised the public to monitor the latest weather forecasts and warnings, avoid flood-prone areas and never attempt to cross floodwaters, while complying with the authorities’ instructions, including evacuation orders when necessary.
Ahmad Zahid also highlighted the importance of being prepared by having important documents, medication, essential supplies and contact numbers ready for emergencies.
“Safety for yourself and your family must come first,” he said, hoping Malaysians would be kept safe from any calamities during the monsoon period. — Bernama

Title: Waze alternatives? Delivery riders, e-hailing drivers wait for TuJu to prove itself
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — For delivery riders and e-hailing drivers who spend hours on the road, switching navigation apps is not as simple as downloading a new one, especially when the routes they take can affect their time, earnings and ability to reach customers.
Outside Sunway Wangsa Walk here, three delivery riders said they had yet to try TuJu, the locally developed navigation app promoted by the government as an alternative to Waze, with some preferring to wait until it becomes more reliable before making the switch.
Muhammad Nabil Khairuddin, 30, a Grab rider, said he first learnt about TuJu through TikTok and Facebook yesterday and was considering downloading it to see how it compared with established navigation apps.
“I might try downloading and using TuJu first to see whether it needs any improvements. I’ll see how it works,” he told
Malay Mail
.
For deliveries, however, Nabil said he already relied on Grab’s in-house navigation system, which allows him to find destinations without leaving the ride-hailing app.
He said Grab previously allowed riders to choose between Waze and Google Maps, but its own navigation system now offered a more convenient option.
“For deliveries, Grab has its own map. Previously, we could choose whether to use Waze or Google Maps, but now Grab has its own navigation system, so there is no need to leave the app. We can navigate directly from there,” he said.
Another rider, who wished to be known as Mat Yo, 32, who works with Lalamove, said he would only consider switching to TuJu once the app was stable, preferring to stick with Waze in the meantime.
“Honestly, Waze is the easiest to use. For Lalamove, it can use Google Maps, but I rarely use it because I’m more comfortable with Waze, it’s easier,” he said.
Mohammad Abdul Aziz Mohd Bhekori, 25, another Grab rider, said he knew little about TuJu and continued to rely on Grab’s map or Google Maps.
Mohammad Abdul Aziz Mohd Bhekori said he knew little about TuJu and continued to rely on Grab’s map or Google Maps. — Picture by Muhammad Yusry
He said he had stopped using Waze previously because it sometimes directed him along what he considered unreasonable routes.
The hesitation among riders comes as the government urges Malaysians to consider uninstalling Waze over concerns that users’ personal and movement data could fall under Israeli jurisdiction.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on October 20, 2026, encouraged the public to use TuJu, developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) in collaboration with Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd, as an alternative to Waze.
National Security Council director-general for National Security Raja Datuk Nushirwan Zainal Abidin has urged Malaysians to uninstall Waze over the concerns.
However, he said that there will not be a blanket ban issued to preserve individual freedom of choice.
For e-hailing drivers, the decision also comes down to familiarity and whether a new app can offer the features they have come to depend on.
A Grab driver of a blue Perodua Bezza, who had just dropped off a passenger at the Sri Rampai LRT station and wished to remain anonymous, said he preferred Waze’s navigation system because it showed toll charges upfront.
Having used Waze for years, he said switching to another app would require time to adjust, but he would consider TuJu if other users gave it positive reviews.
“If people start saying that TuJu is good, then I’ll use it,” he said.
Muhammad Khalid Azmi, 28, an e-hailing driver based in Putrajaya, said he had not tried TuJu and would continue using Waze, with Google Maps as an alternative.
Khalid, who has used Waze for more than five years, said he relied on it to check traffic conditions, estimated arrival times and journey durations.
He also found Grab’s navigation system useful, saying it could incorporate community feedback and updates, while the map available on Bolt was less accurate in his experience.
“I haven’t used TuJu yet, so I don’t know what it is like, or what its weaknesses and strengths are. For now, I prefer either Waze or Google Maps because Grab has its own in-house map, which works reasonably well.
“However, when I’m using Bolt, its map is not accurate. The established navigation apps are either Google Maps and Waze. I’m not sure about the other navigation apps, but those two are already linked to e-hailing apps,” he said.
TuJu, which was launched in November last year, provides navigation, estimated arrival times, live traffic information, highway CCTV feeds, toll fares and information on rest and service areas.
However, the app has faced technical disruptions following a surge in users after Anwar recommended it as an alternative to Waze.
LLM and PCSB apologised for the disruption, saying they were working to restore system stability, increase capacity and address complaints about navigation functions, route accuracy and the overall user experience.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said that the government was also expanding TuJu’s coverage beyond highways to include ordinary roads, following public feedback calling for more comprehensive navigation services.
The expansion is intended to improve traffic information and the app’s overall capabilities, as the government seeks to strengthen the use of locally developed technology.
For riders and drivers who depend on navigation throughout the working day, however, TuJu will have to prove itself on the road before it can displace the apps they already know and trust.

Title: Fresher air in Malaysia again: Only Samalaju in Sarawak still unhealthy after months of haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Malaysia is breathing easier today, with only one place in the country still recording unhealthy air after a haze season that began in August.
Samalaju in Sarawak is the lone station in the unhealthy range, with its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading edging up to 152 at 9am from 151 at 7am, according to the Department of Environment’s Malaysia Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) website.
All Klang Valley readings were below 100 at 9am, with some places in the “good” category.
Banting (45) and Kuala Selangor (47) were rated “good”, while Petaling Jaya (52), Shah Alam (54), Klang (58) and Johan Setia (66) were moderate.
Putrajaya recorded 54, while Cheras read 58 and Batu Muda 84 — the highest of the Klang Valley readings.
It is a sharp turnaround from August 28, when six of the 19 unhealthy stations nationwide were in the Greater Klang Valley, with Cheras at 160.
The smog was then thick enough that the government moved the National Day Prime Minister’s Address from Dataran Merdeka to the indoor Putrajaya International Convention Centre.
Johor, which had been struggling with high pollution levels, saw all its stations read below 100 at 9am.
An API reading of zero to 50 is considered good, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy and above 300 hazardous.

Title: The Pacific and HIV: A chance to turn the tide — Eamonn Murphy, Saia Ma’u Piukala, Pio Smith, Beate Trankmann and Delphine Schantz
Article:
