OCT 27 — The world has spent more than 40 years learning what works in the AIDS response. For the Pacific, with its long tradition of collective action in tackling shared challenges, those hard-won lessons could help prevent today’s growing HIV epidemics from becoming a much larger crisis.
The recent surge of international attention to Fiji’s HIV epidemic has carried uncomfortable echoes of an earlier era of AIDS.
A rapid rise in new infections. A national crisis declaration. Stories of people struggling to access services or staying away because of pervasive stigma. Health systems racing to catch up with an epidemic moving faster than the response. Once again, HIV has made international headlines with an urgency many had hoped belonged to the past.
But there is one fundamental difference. This is 2026.
Today, we have effective treatment, powerful new prevention tools and decades of experience that did not exist at the start of the AIDS epidemic. The Pacific cannot afford to lose time or repeat past mistakes.
The need to act is urgent: Fiji has seen one of the fastest-growing HIV epidemics globally, with new infections rising approximately twelvefold between 2010 and 2025. But Fiji is not the only warning sign. Papua New Guinea remains the largest HIV epidemic in the region, with an estimated 110,000 people living with HIV. HIV diagnoses have also risen recently in Palau, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu. Across the Pacific, new infections increased by an estimated 65 per cent between 2010 and 2025, while they declined across Asia and the Pacific overall.
In countries with small populations, even relatively few new infections can signal a major shift in the epidemic. Waiting until the numbers become alarming means losing valuable time to prevent further transmission.
Today, we have effective treatment, powerful new prevention tools and decades of experience that did not exist at the start of the AIDS epidemic. The Pacific cannot afford to lose time or repeat past mistakes. — AFP file pic
First, HIV is everyone’s concern
In 1989, American artist and activist Keith Haring painted a mural: Todos juntos podemos parar el sida—Together We Can Stop AIDS. More than a slogan, it captured the spirit of a movement that brought together people who had rarely worked side by side: doctors and politicians, activists and scientists, faith leaders and teachers, police and community advocates, celebrities and people living with HIV.
That mobilisation required heads of state to speak publicly about AIDS, parliaments to change laws that fuelled stigma or blocked access to services, and societies to confront deep-seated prejudice. The early AIDS response showed how fear and misinformation can contribute to discrimination—a lesson worth bearing in mind when measures such as mandatory testing or restrictive border controls are considered. It also demanded action across sectors: from health and education to law enforcement and justice, alongside broader efforts to advance human rights, gender equality and development.
Fiji’s declaration of a national HIV crisis is an important political step. It recognises that the health sector cannot tackle the epidemic alone.
Across the Pacific, addressing discriminatory laws, stigma and other barriers to prevention and treatment requires the kind of political leadership and collective action that shaped the global AIDS response.
Second, let communities lead
The AIDS response was transformed by the communities most affected by HIV. They challenged stigma, fought for access to treatment and helped shape services around people’s needs.
Even today, despite advances in treatment and prevention, stigma and discrimination still keep many people away from HIV services. Fear of judgement or unwanted disclosure can determine whether someone seeks testing or treatment at all.
Community organisations and peer outreach workers help bridge that gap by building trust and reaching people who might otherwise remain outside the health system. This is especially important in the Pacific, where small island communities and remote settings can make privacy harder to protect and confidentiality all the more important.
As Pacific countries move towards greater national ownership and sustainable financing, community-led services need to become an integral part of national HIV plans and budgets, rather than remain dependent on short-term donor-funded projects. With external funding under pressure, this transition must not come at the cost of prevention, or of the independence and trust that make these services effective.
Third, close the gap between progress and access
Medical science has transformed what is possible. Antiretroviral treatment now enables people living with HIV to lead long, healthy lives.
When people take effective antiretroviral treatment and achieve and maintain an undetectable viral load, they do not transmit HIV sexually—the principle known as U=U, or Undetectable = Untransmittable.
Yet treatment coverage remains alarmingly low in parts of the Pacific. In Fiji, only about a quarter of the total estimated people living with HIV accessed treatment, and in Papua New Guinea, only about half.
Effective treatment during pregnancy and breastfeeding can protect women’s health and prevent HIV transmission to their babies. In Papua New Guinea, however, only about one in four pregnant women living with HIV receive antiretroviral treatment, and an estimated 2,700 infants acquired HIV in 2024—a stark reminder of the distance that can remain between what medicine makes possible and what reaches families in time. That is why HIV testing and treatment need to be readily accessible through routine antenatal, maternal and child health services, including in remote communities.
Prevention has entered a new era too. In countries where injecting drug use is one of the risks driving increasing HIV cases, needle and syringe programmes play a critical role in preventing needle sharing—something that poses very high risks for HIV spread. These programmes don’t just protect people who inject drugs; they also protect their loved ones, and the broader community.
Alongside proven approaches such as condoms, harm reduction and oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir offers an important new option, particularly for people who find taking a daily pill difficult.
Prevention is increasingly about choice: matching proven options to people’s needs and lives. In Fiji, where HIV infections linked to injecting drug use are increasing, recent legal changes have made it possible to introduce a needle and syringe programme—showing how prevention can adapt as the epidemic changes.
But none of these advances can prevent infections or save lives if people cannot access them. New prevention and treatment options need to reach Pacific countries sooner, at prices they can afford.
Access is about more than medicines. Many Pacific nations already face shortages of health workers, limited resources and the high costs of delivering care across remote islands. Climate change adds to these pressures, as extreme weather threatens health facilities and disrupts essential services.
As countries expand their HIV responses, prevention, testing and treatment can be integrated into primary health care and other essential services rather than built as costly parallel systems. This can make care easier to access, use scarce resources more effectively and strengthen health systems for the future, while preserving the specialised and community-led services that people trust.
Services also need to reach people who are often missed, including people in prisons, and ensure continuity of prevention, treatment and care when they return to the community.
For smaller Pacific countries, greater national ownership cannot mean going it alone. Sustained international financing will still be needed alongside growing domestic investment. Regional cooperation can help those resources go further—through pooled procurement, stronger supply chains and shared expertise. Not every country needs to build every service or specialist capability from scratch.
Pacific institutions such as the Pacific Community (SPC), working alongside the UN Joint Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)—including UNDP, UNFPA, UNODC and WHO—can help countries put these shared solutions into practice, bringing governments, communities and development partners together around national priorities.
An opportunity the Pacific cannot afford to miss
Only four years remain until 2030, the target year set by UN Member States for ending AIDS as a public health threat. The UN Political Declaration on HIV/AIDS, adopted in June 2026, renewed commitments to prevention and treatment, human rights, community leadership and sustainable financing.
The Pacific has the knowledge, the tools and a strong history of collective action. What happens next will shape the region’s HIV epidemics for years to come.
Fiji’s experience is a warning for the entire region. But it can also become a turning point.
*Eamonn Murphy is UNAIDS Regional Director for Asia and the Pacific and Eastern Europe and Central Asia; Dr Saia Ma’u Piukala is WHO Regional Director for the Western Pacific; Pio Smith is UNFPA Regional Director for Asia and the Pacific; Beate Trankmann is UNDP Deputy Regional Director for Asia and the Pacific and Director of the Bangkok Regional Hub; and Delphine Schantz is UNODC Regional Representative for Southeast Asia and the Pacific.

Title: Nancy Shukri warns withholding money for basic needs can amount to domestic abuse, urges victims to seek help
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Being denied money for clothing, reprimanded over online purchases or forced to rely entirely on a partner for personal needs are among the situations that may constitute economic abuse within a household.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said domestic violence extended beyond physical and emotional abuse to include economic control, which could affect a victim’s well-being and self-confidence.
She said this form of abuse warranted attention as it could occur in everyday situations, such as when a partner failed to provide money for basic family necessities or controlled personal spending, leaving the victim without financial autonomy.
“For example, a husband returns home expecting his wife to prepare a meal. If she is not working and has no money of her own, and he fails to provide funds for household necessities, how is she supposed to cook?
“Another example is when a wife wants to buy clothes but does not have the means to do so, leaving her unable to shop like other women. If she orders items online, she may end up being scolded by her husband. This is a common occurrence and has become a new challenge in life today,” she said during an appearance on
Bernama TV’s
Ruang Bicara programme here last night.
Nancy said such financial control could strip victims of the freedom to make decisions about their own needs, particularly if they had no income or access to funds.
According to her, police statistics showed an increase in domestic violence cases, from 5,507 in 2023 to 7,016 in 2024 and 7,391 in 2025, with 5,278 cases recorded from January to August this year.
“Domestic violence can take various forms and occur in different situations, but the challenge arises when victims choose to remain silent and do not seek help. In some cases, even after lodging a report, they later withdraw it out of fear,” she said.
In this regard, Nancy said the ministry provided various forms of support to help victims escape abusive situations and rebuild their lives, including counselling services, intervention measures and financial assistance to attend court proceedings if necessary.
She stressed that addressing domestic violence was also vital to protect children who witnessed abuse at home, as such experiences could influence how they viewed family relationships as they grew older.
“We do not want children who witness such behaviour to grow up and repeat it because they have come to view it as normal,” she said.
Nancy therefore urged the public not to treat domestic violence as merely a private family matter, but to report any known or suspected incidents by calling Talian Kasih at 15999 or sending a WhatsApp message to 019-2615999. — Bernama

Title: Durian orchard that never was: CEO to face charge over RM1.65m scam in Shah Alam court today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The chief executive officer of a fruit and vegetable wholesale, import and export company is expected to be charged today over a durian orchard purchase scam involving about RM1.65 million, the
New Straits Times
reported.
The man, in his 50s, was arrested at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) headquarters in Putrajaya at 12pm yesterday after giving his statement.
Initial investigations showed the offence took place in February 2024, but the orchard purchase never materialised, a source told the newspaper.
MACC chief Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrest.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code, and the suspect will be charged in court in Shah Alam, Selangor today.
The MACC previously launched Op Kingfruit over a durian investment scam in Raub, Pahang, freezing bank accounts and seizing assets worth RM16.15 million.

Title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Health commission, hospital overcrowding and disaster risk mapping among key issues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The proposed Health Services Commission, overcrowding at government hospitals and measures to strengthen disaster risk mapping in Malaysia are among the issues scheduled to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper published on Parliament’s website, Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa (PH-Sekijang) will ask the Health Minister to state the ministry’s commitment to tabling the proposed Health Services Commission Bill for first reading before the end of 2027, in line with the reform aspirations outlined in the 2023 Health White Paper.
Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun (PH-Port Dickson) will seek an explanation from the Health Minister on persistent overcrowding at emergency departments, including average patient waiting times and concrete measures to ease congestion and ensure patients receive timely treatment.
Also on the agenda is a question from Datuk Verdon Bahanda (Independent-Kudat), who will ask the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister about measures to strengthen disaster risk mapping in Malaysia and how the latest risk data is being used to improve early warning systems, development planning and disaster preparedness.
Meanwhile, Tan Kok Wai (PH-Cheras) will ask the Investment, Trade and Industry Minister to provide the total number and a detailed list of projects realised from Geely’s US$10 billion investment commitment in Tanjung Malim.
Khairil Nizam Khirudin (PN-Jerantut) will seek clarification from the Transport Minister on the postponement of the enforcement of Speed Limitation Device (SLD) installation requirements and the government’s assessment of a proposal to re-establish the Land Public Transport Commission (SPAD).
During the Minister’s Question Time, Syahredzan Johan (PH-Bangi) will ask the Prime Minister to explain the rationale behind involving government departments, government-linked investment companies (GLICs), government-linked companies (GLCs) and statutory bodies in the implementation of development projects.
Datuk Che Mohamad Zulkifly Jusoh (PN-Besut) will also ask the Prime Minister to outline the formula and criteria used by the government to determine the allocation of constituency development funds (CDF) to Members of Parliament. — Bernama

Title: TuJu built for stranded motorists on expressways, not to rival Waze, says highway authority chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — TuJu was never meant to rival Waze, Malaysian Highway Authority chairman Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad has said.
His clarification comes after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim urged Malaysian civil servants to switch to the local app over security concerns linked to Waze’s Israeli ties.
“It is not a navigation application like Waze,” Hasni, who is also Simpang Renggam MP, told
Malaysiakini
in an interview published today.
He said TuJu was conceived as an added service for tolled highway users, offering traffic updates, rest area details, enforcement camera locations and emergency contacts, stressing that its real value, Hasni said, lies when the vehicle breaks down.
“If you are stranded on a highway, you can use TuJu to find the telephone numbers of people you can contact and the assistance available,” he was quoted as saying.
He added that the prime minister has told him to upgrade the app, which drew complaints of glitches after a surge in downloads.
Anwar admitted on October 23 that the local navigation app was incomplete.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo have since stressed that TuJu is not compulsory for all Malaysians and that alternatives such as Google Maps remain permissible.
Hasni said he missed the October 20 National Security Council briefing but has read its minutes.
He wants to establish whether the highway authority, better known as LLM – its abbreviation in Malay, short for Lembaga Lebuhraya Malaysia –  and developer Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd explained the app’s purpose clearly.
“If the briefing given by LLM to the NSC was misleading, it should not have happened,” he was quoted as saying.
Scrutiny has also fallen on Prosignal’s ties to former LLM chairman Datuk Abdul Rashid Asari, who told Malaysiakini he proposed the project and confirmed it was not awarded through an open tender.
Hasni, who is also an Umno supreme council member, said the LLM board approved the project collectively, stressing: “It was not his decision alone”.
“TuJu is financed by investors in the project, whether through internal funds or loans,” he replied when asked about the lack of a tender, signalling that no government money was involved.
Asked whether TuJu was earning income for LLM, Hasni said he would need to check the project’s return-on-investment projections.

Title: Two motorcyclists killed in three-vehicle crash on Johor Bahru-Gelang Patah road
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 27 — Two motorcyclists were killed in a collision involving three vehicles at Kilometre 24.9 of the Johor Bahru-Gelang Patah-Pendas Road here yesterday morning.
Iskandar Puteri District Police Chief ACP Radin Ramlan Radin Taha said that at about 7.20 am, a car carrying a driver and two passengers was travelling towards Lima Kedai.
He said the car was believed to have lost control while negotiating a bend on a wet and slippery road before veering into the opposite lane and colliding with two motorcycles travelling from the direction of Gelang Patah.
“Both motorcyclists, local men aged 34 and 50, were pronounced dead at the scene after sustaining severe injuries to their heads and right legs.
“The bodies were sent to Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) in Johor Bahru for post-mortems, while the car driver and two passengers sustained minor injuries to their heads, faces and right legs,” he said in a statement tonight.
Radin Ramlan said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, and members of the public or witnesses with information about the incident were urged to come forward to assist in the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Super El Nino threat: Govt steps up measures to protect padi supply, fisheries as heat and drought loom
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM) has stepped up inter-agency preparedness measures to address the Super El Nino phenomenon, which is already showing early effects in the country.
Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the national agrofood sector was facing mounting challenges due to the conflict in West Asia and the threat of extreme heat and prolonged dry weather, which could disrupt the supply of staple foods.
He said particular attention was being given to monitoring dam water levels, especially at the Ahning Dam in Kedah, where levels remained at alert and warning thresholds, posing a risk to padi cultivation in the major Muda granary area.
“The ministry has mobilised inter-agency preparedness measures through an integrated approach and the use of technology.
“These include implementing Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM), expanding the Smart Irrigation Monitoring System, introducing alternative water management methods for padi cultivation and promoting Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) to ensure sustainable water security,” he said when winding up debate on the Supply Bill 2027 for the ministry in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
Mohamad said extensive preparations were also under way in the fisheries sector, as rising sea temperatures were altering fish distribution patterns, affecting aquaculture water quality and threatening reef ecosystems.
He said capture fisheries and aquaculture production in affected areas could decline by 5,624 metric tonnes, or 1.5 per cent, this year.
To address these challenges, he said the ministry had taken proactive measures, including the use of early weather warning systems, the MyFSI location tracking system and the Aquaculture Disaster Mitigation Plan, alongside the implementation of the Fisheries Sector Climate Change Action Plan 2024-2030.
“Under Budget 2027, RM125.9 million in fiscal support has been allocated, including RM30 million for an additional 3,000 special small-boat licences, RM30 million for Agro BioFloc financing, RM10 million for Capture Fisheries Catalyst Financing and RM2.3 million for biofisheries and biosecurity initiatives,” he said.
Meanwhile, Mohamad assured that the country’s frozen fish reserves were being increased, with total stocks reaching 10,000 metric tonnes as of Sept 30 to prepare for the Super El Nino phenomenon and the Northeast Monsoon.
Overall, he said the ministry received an allocation of RM6.92 billion under Budget 2027, comprising RM4.85 billion for operating expenditure and RM2.07 billion for development expenditure.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting continues today. — Bernama

Title: Felda settler hacked to death with axe in Johor rampage
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Oct 27 — A Felda settler was hacked to death with an axe in an alleged violent rampage at Felda Lok Heng Selatan here last night.
The incident is understood to have occurred at about 7.30pm after the male suspect allegedly ran amok near his residence.
Armed with an axe, the suspect attacked the victim by the roadside.
The incident drew the attention of other residents before the suspect fled on a motorcycle.
Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said police were investigating the incident.
He said police would issue an official statement on the incident today.

Title: Three men arrested after firefighter dies in Port Dickson hit-and-run, driver allegedly fled scene
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 27 — Police have arrested three local men to assist in investigations into a fatal accident involving a firefighter at KM2.6 of Jalan Pantai, Port Dickson, this morning.
Port Dickson police chief, Supt Ahmad Afiq Mohd Adnan, said that the three men, aged 31 and 32, comprised the driver of a Toyota Vios and two friends, who allegedly conspired to hide the car in Puchong, Selangor, and remove its registration number plates.
He said that at about 8.05 am, the victim, a 46-year-old man riding a Honda ADV160 motorcycle, and the car were believed to have been travelling from Telok Kemang towards Port Dickson.
“Upon reaching the scene, the car is believed to have made a U-turn, causing the motorcyclist, who was behind it, to try to avoid the vehicle before crashing into its right side and falling onto the opposite lane.
“The victim sustained serious injuries and was pronounced dead while receiving treatment at the Emergency Ward of Port Dickson Hospital, while the car driver fled the scene after the accident,” he said in a statement here last night.
Ahmad Afiq added that the car driver was subsequently arrested at the Serdang police headquarters at about 6.30 pm today, while his two friends were arrested in Puchong.
Checks found that the driver did not have a valid driving licence, while the vehicle’s road tax and insurance had expired.
He said that the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, and an application for a remand order against all three men will be made at the Port Dickson Court today. — Bernama

Title: Fire and Rescue Department mobilises 25,592 personnel, 1,248 assets ahead of Northeast Monsoon
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — A total of 25,592 officers and personnel of the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), along with 1,248 assets, are on standby to face the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL), which is expected to begin tomorrow and last until March next year.
JBPM director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the department had strengthened its operational planning by ensuring personnel availability, asset and logistical readiness, and the strategic deployment of resources to deal with possible disasters throughout the period.
He added that during the initial phase of the monsoon, from November this year to January next year, three to five episodes of continuous heavy rain were expected, potentially increasing the risk of flooding in low-lying areas and locations near rivers.
The conditions could also cause rough seas and rising sea levels in the South China Sea, due to persistent northeast winds.
“Our priority is public safety. JBPM has formulated a comprehensive response strategy covering prevention and mitigation, planning and preparedness, emergency response, and post-disaster recovery,” he said in a statement here yesterday.
In planning its operational preparedness, JBPM had taken into account 3,682 flood hotspots identified nationwide, based on data from the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID). The data would serve as a guide in determining the priority deployment of personnel and assets, according to risk levels and on-the-ground requirements.
He said to expedite response efforts in high-risk areas, 29 Rapid Response Teams (PGC) had been mobilised, while Regional Forward Bases (RFB) in Penang, Terengganu and Johor had been activated to facilitate the deployment of personnel and assets to locations requiring assistance.
“In terms of personnel, JBPM’s preparedness plan includes 13,631 full-time fire officers (PSM), 2,227 Auxiliary Fire Officers (PBB), 8,956 Volunteer Fire Brigade (PBS) members and 62 engineering personnel.
“Leave restrictions of between 80 and 100 per cent have also been imposed, according to operational needs, particularly in states at risk of being affected, to ensure sufficient personnel are available,” he said.
Meanwhile, he said rapid response capabilities had also been strengthened through the involvement of the Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) and the Water Rescue Team (PPDA) to provide emergency medical assistance and carry out flood rescue operations.
“JBPM has also prepared 571 light transport vehicles, 144 heavy transport vehicles and 529 marine assets, in addition to four helicopters and three drones, to support rescue operations. It has also provided 150 community boats to help local residents take early action during emergencies, with due consideration given to safety,” he said.
Nor Hisham said that, apart from flood risks, JBPM was also monitoring expected weather changes during the final phase of the Northeast Monsoon, from January to March next year, when rainfall is expected to decrease, particularly in the northern part of the Peninsula and Sabah. Meanwhile, the influence of a very strong El Nino phenomenon could lead to hotter and drier conditions, and a higher risk of more extreme heatwaves.
“JBPM will continue to strengthen its preparedness and cooperation with relevant agencies to ensure that rescue operations and emergency assistance can be carried out efficiently and effectively, to protect lives, public safety and property throughout the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi: RM5b Jendela revamp to use Starlink, small cells to close Malaysia’s final 1pc Internet coverage gap
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The National Digital Network (Jendela) initiative is being modified to use alternative technologies such as Starlink and small cells to achieve 100 per cent Internet coverage in populated areas, says Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzi.
He said the strategic shift is backed by an allocation of RM5 billion over several years to ensure hard-to-reach rural areas are not left behind.
“We might not build telecommunication towers everywhere. In some places, we will install Starlink, in others, small cells sufficient for the 40 to 50 people living there. The goal is to ensure 100 per cent coverage in populated areas, including the most remote locations.
“Building a tower is costly, so we will deploy solutions better suited to the community. As the community grows, we can upgrade the technology later,” he said when appearing as a guest on the Agenda AWANI talk show titled ‘Belanjawan 2027: Rapatkan Jurang Digital, Pacu Ekonomi Kreatif’ last night.
He said Internet coverage in populated areas has currently reached 99 per cent, and the remaining one per cent requires more practical solutions tailored to the size of local communities.
“We also noticed another issue. In many Felda settlements, the coverage is good, but once you get onto the trunk roads connecting these settlements to towns, there is often no signal.
“This poses a danger, so Jendela will focus on equipping such areas with coverage,” he said.
Apart from remote settlements, Fahmi said the restructuring of the Jendela initiative also marked a paradigm shift from solely focusing on Coverage of Populated Areas (COPA) to Economic Area Coverage.
He added that comprehensive connectivity would be bolstered by an RM142 million allocation to empower 1,099 National Information Dissemination Centres (NADI) nationwide.
However, he stressed that the high-speed Internet infrastructure provided by the government must go hand-in-hand with high digital literacy and security awareness among the public to curb cybercrime and online scams.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said the creative sector, also known as the orange economy, has tremendous potential to emerge as a key driver of the country’s economic growth.
He said the sector’s reported 6.8 per cent contribution to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) proves its massive capability as a highly viable economic asset, particularly in animation, online gaming, and film.
“With this budget, the formation of the Orange Economy Council, and the growth rate of specific segments within the creative economy, the future of this sector is very bright.
“It forms a huge part of the national economy. The sectors showing the most vibrant growth and are easiest to export include animated films, online gaming, and e-sports,” he said.
He noted that Malaysia is among the most active countries in the animation sector and has become a hub for producing animation for foreign markets.
Fahmi also highlighted the success of five Malaysian animation studios that recently participated in the prestigious Annecy International Animation Film Festival in France, bringing home over RM250 million in investments with the support of the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (FINAS). — Bernama

Title: Bukit Aman seizes RM765,750 in unregistered health products, suspected counterfeit goods in KL raid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 —The Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence (WCB/PSK) unit of Bukit Aman’s Internal Security and Public Order Department seized unregistered health and cosmetic products alongside suspected counterfeit branded goods worth RM765,750 during a raid on a courier company’s premises here this morning.
WCB/PSK commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said the 10.50 am raid was carried out jointly with the Health Ministry’s (MOH) Pharmacy Enforcement Division and the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN).
He said the integrated operation resulted in the seizure of 9,257 units of health products, cosmetics, and branded goods suspected of violating statutory regulations.
“The courier and logistics company’s premises was suspected of being used as a storage and distribution hub for health products, cosmetics, and branded goods believed not to comply with legal requirements.
“Two foreign men, aged 23 and 29, believed to be working as packers at the premises, were also detained on suspicion of committing immigration offences,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Mohd Zaki said further inspection uncovered 9,130 units of various brands of health and cosmetic products suspected of not being registered with MOH, as well as 127 branded items suspected of bearing counterfeit trademarks.
“Of the total seizure, the health and cosmetic products, valued at an estimated RM734,000, were acted upon by MOH’s Pharmacy Enforcement Division, while the suspected counterfeit goods, valued at RM31,750, were seized by KPDN.
“The case is being investigated under Regulation 7(1)(a) and Regulation 18A of the Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984, as well as Section 102 of the Trademarks Act 2019, while the two foreign nationals are being investigated under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63,” he said.
Mohd Zaki added that from Jan 1 to date, the unit has conducted 286 raids nationwide and arrested 467 individuals for various offences involving the smuggling of contraband, leakages of controlled and subsidised goods, wildlife trafficking, and operations related to electronic waste (e-waste).
“During the same period, the total value of seizures recorded is estimated at RM335,963,935.42,” he said. — Bernama

Title: PH to highlight Anwar govt’s welfare aid and security record in Melaka election campaign, says Saifuddin
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 27 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) will implement a prudent campaign in the Melaka State Election (PRN) by explaining the Unity Government’s initiatives under the leadership of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to the rakyat.
Home Minister and Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Vice President Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the successes and welfare initiatives implemented by the government must be conveyed in the best possible way to voters so that they are confident in choosing candidates from PH.
“We do not want to win an election campaign through hurling insults and cursing, we do not want that. That is not PKR’s way... we do not want to win elections through instigating conflict and division... let other parties do that if they want to win that way, please go ahead.
“Our politics is different. Our politics is one that invites peace, love, and unity. Only then does politics have value. Only then does politics possess the nature of worship (ibadah),” he said when speaking at the inauguration of the Paya Rumput State Legislative Assembly Operations Room in Krubong here last night.
Also present were Melaka PKR State Leadership Council (MPN) Acting Chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim and the PH candidate for the Paya Rumput DUN seat, Datuk Azman Abidin.
Saifuddin Nasution stated that among these successes is Malaysia’s current standing as the 12th safest country in the world to visit, which proves the government’s capability in controlling national security.
In addition, the RM200 schooling assistance for 5.2 million students and pupils nationwide can touch voters’ hearts through the welfare agenda implemented by the government.
“If there are three children, (one family gets) RM600 in cash. School uniforms, school shoes, sports attire, school bags, school supplies, insya-Allah, are covered. Parents no longer have to worry.
“The Prime Minister helps think about (school-related problems) and helps solve them. That is a small example that sticks and is felt by every household because they have school-going children,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: RM150m allocated to complete 554 Felda new-generation homes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The government has allocated an additional RM150 million to complete three Felda New Generation Housing Projects (PGBF) involving 554 housing units.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the projects, comprising 200 units each at Felda Bukit Aping Timur and Felda Pasak, and 154 units at Felda Kerteh 5, were announced during Felda Settlers’ Day on July 7.
On the Rumah Pahang housing project at Felda Jengka 11, he said it had been fully handed over to the Pahang government, specifically through the Pahang Housing and Property Board (LPHP).
“The project was 75 per cent complete in 2025 and is currently undergoing maintenance under the supervision of the relevant authorities,” he said in a written reply published on Parliament’s official website yesterday.
He was replying to a question from Kamal Ashaari (PN-Kuala Krau).
Anwar added that the PGBF programme began in 2013, with a total of 2,458 housing units across 12 project sites completed and occupied by eligible second-generation Felda settlers. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia compiling nationwide refugee data under new registration programme, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The government is compiling data on refugee communities nationwide through the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme under National Security Council (MKN) Directive No. 23, says Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said the programme, currently in its first phase, focuses on individuals held at Immigration Detention Depots (DTI).
The initiative is expected to progress soon to its second phase, focusing on United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cardholders residing outside the depots, he added.
“The data collection aims to ensure the government can manage, coordinate, and monitor the temporary presence of these individuals in the country before they are resettled in a third country or repatriated to their country of origin,” he said in a written reply published on the Parliament website last night.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, was replying to a question from Mohd Sany Hamzan (PH-Hulu Langat) on the government’s stance regarding foreign organisations operating in Malaysia, such as UNHCR, amid claims that the agency has not provided expected cooperation and refused to share data on refugees.
Ahmad Zahid said international organisations remain essential to Malaysia as platforms for cooperation and expertise sharing to tackle cross-border issues that cannot be handled unilaterally, while building national capacity and easing the burden of managing humanitarian challenges.
He noted that this position is reflected in Malaysia’s experience in handling Vietnamese refugees on Pulau Bidong from the late 1970s to the 1990s, when Malaysia collaborated with UNHCR and the international community to manage refugee influxes, provide temporary shelter, and secure third-country resettlement.
“At present, the government also requires UNHCR to facilitate third-country resettlement, as recipient nations rely on the UNHCR card to verify and authenticate refugees,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Disaster Risk Reduction Act study expected to be completed within 12 months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The baseline study on the proposed Disaster Risk Reduction Act, following the proposal for the National Disaster Management Bill, is expected to be completed within 12 months.
Deputy Prime Minister, Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, said that the findings and recommendations of the study, conducted by the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), would be reviewed and coordinated with the relevant ministries and agencies before the proposed policy and legislation were finalised.
“At present, a specific timeline for the tabling of the National Disaster Management Bill in the Dewan Rakyat has yet to be determined.
“This is because the current process still involves reviewing the need for, and the appropriate form of, the legislative framework,” he said in a written reply published on the Parliament website last night.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, was responding to a question from Zahir Hassan (PH-Wangsa Maju), who wanted to know the latest developments in the drafting of the National Disaster Management Bill.
Ahmad Zahid said that the findings of the study would serve as an important basis for Nadma in determining the direction of efforts to strengthen the country’s disaster governance, particularly in terms of prevention, risk reduction and enhancing the resilience of communities and the nation.
“The government is taking an approach to ensure that the form and scope of the proposed legislation are truly suited to the country’s disaster management needs, rather than simply enacting a new law without first identifying the actual gaps in the existing framework.
“This approach is also in line with the country’s disaster management direction, which emphasises science-, data- and technology-based preparedness, early action, early warning systems, clear command structures, and rapid and coordinated responses,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Want to plan your finances to have enough for retirement in Malaysia? Here are some tips
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — As the average life expectancy of Malaysians rise, the pressing question becomes whether they are equipped financially to live past retirement.
Based on Malaysia’s latest official figures, babies born in 2026 are expected to live to 75.5, while a person aged 60 and 65 now are expected to live to 80.2 and 81.5 respectively.
In an interview with
Malay Mail
, licensed financial planner Rajen Devadason said, “But what are you going to do if you live to be 85, 90, 95, 100, 105?”
In planning for your retirement finances, Rajen said you could split your net income (after paying taxes) into three portions of about 33 per cent each:
Past (Money that you have already spent, but are paying now = Existing debts, e.g. housing loan, car loan)
Present (Current expenses = What you have to pay for today)
Future (What you have to invest now for the future)
“You should probably commit one third to pay your debts, try and accelerate that, get rid of those as fast as possible; one third to take care of your middle section, your current expenses; and one third for tomorrow,” he told
Malay Mail
at the Employees Provident Fund’s (EPF) recent International Social Wellbeing Conference 2026 (ISWC 2026).
If you are currently contributing 11 per cent to your EPF retirement savings, Rajen said this means you would need to put aside about another 22 per cent into sources that can generate passive income for the future.
Rajen listed some common passive income sources:
Interest from money in the bank;
Dividends from EPF savings or from dividend-paying stocks;
Cash distributions from unit trust investments;
Rental income collected from properties you own (such as apartment, shoplot);
Listed Real Estate Investment Trusts (REIT) and REIT funds.
Once you have cleared off your debts, you can then spend half of your income on current expenses and preparing for the future, he suggested.
Rajen said he gives this advice to his clients too: “Then it’s really up to them. They’re the ones who are going to have to work on their budget. They need to have a written budget.
“They need to work harder, work longer, work smarter to increase their active income, their earned income. That can be salaries or business revenue.
“And then they need to control their expenses; create the surplus; and then they need to allocate the surplus,” he said, highlighting the importance of using the extra money to create multiple pipelines of passive income.
He stressed the need to take “personal responsibility” for your own finances and to create your own pension or retirement income, instead of expecting the government to take care of you.
Rajen Devadason said delaying gratification now often means giving up what is ‘good’ now for what is ‘great down the road’, which in this case would be building up financial reserves for retirement. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Skip the lifestyle upgrades now for better cash flow, so you can be less stressed in the future
At ISWC 2026, Rajen said one key step is to get off the “hedonic treadmill” — or the cycle where a new lifestyle upgrade becomes the new norm, and you then spend increasingly more money to buy the next lifestyle upgrade.
“Now if you do this at a younger age, you’ll actually have more time to generate surpluses to take advantage of compounding,” he said, as you would have better cash flow or more money available to build up passive income.
He noted that the lack of passive income causes great stress during retirement, where people see their pool of money “evaporate” due to inflation, living expenses, emergencies, medical costs or vacations.
Choosing to delay gratification now and to create passive income would help with reducing that stress, he said.
Apart from building up financial reserves for retirement, Rajen said Malaysians should also build up their cognitive reserves and try to “stay mentally sharp for as long as possible so that you don’t lose control of the cerebral capacity to be able to manage your money”.
How old do you think you will live and when should you retire?
Rajen added that the longevity risk that people face globally is the risk of people living longer than their money lasts.
He suggested one way to work out what age you might likely live to: Get an average of how long your parents’ families have lived, and add another five years.
He recommended working past the official retirement age if necessary to hit retirement income goals.
“I recommend that regardless of what age you have to keep working to, do not retire until you have paid off all your debts,” he also said, adding that it would then be easier to manage finances.
Malaysia’s retirement age is currently 60, and Rajen has proposed to gradually raise it to 65 by the year 2035, and to 70 by the year 2050.
JP Morgan Asset Management’s chief market strategist (Asia Pacific) Tai Hui said it would be easier to work out what investment plans you should use after you have a retirement income goal. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Work backwards from a retirement goal
At an ISWC 2026 panel session, JP Morgan Asset Management’s chief market strategist (Asia Pacific) Tai Hui proposed setting your retirement goal first, such as what you want to achieve at 65.
“I think the important thing is to start calculating roughly how much you need when you retire to live a comfortable life to cover your expenses, your contingencies.
“And then sort of work backwards, how much you got to save, how much you got to invest, what should you be investing in?” he said.
Currently, EPF’s Retirement Income Adequacy (RIA) framework sets out what Malaysians can target to save up in EPF by age 60: Basic Savings Level (RM390,000), Adequate Savings Level (RM650,000), or Enhanced Savings Level (RM1.3 million).
Kickstart your retirement planning today
If you still don’t know where to start, you can try:
Visiting your nearest EPF branch to get free financial planning and retirement planning advice from their Relationship & Advisory service
EPF’s Retirement Goal Calculator to set your retirement savings goal
(It’s really easy to use. Just sign in to EPF’s i-Akaun app for an estimate of how long your savings can last during retirement, and how much more you may need to save.)

Title: Budget 2027 autism initiatives aim to bridge early education gap for rural, low-income children
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 27 — Access to appropriate early education and guidance is essential for autistic children, particularly those from low-income families and rural communities, to help them develop their potential early on.
Against this backdrop, plans under Budget 2027 to build two Permata Kurnia centres in Pahang and Melaka and open 130 new Tabika Tunas Istimewa classes in rural areas nationwide are expected to give more children access to education and support suited to their individual needs.
Malaysian Childcare Centre Association founder and chairman Ng Chun Piew said the initiatives could widen access to early guidance, but their success would hinge on appropriate facilities, trained teachers and quality services.
He said stronger cooperation among the government, experts, parents and childcare providers was essential to ensure autistic children received the support they needed for their development and well-being.
“We hope the new centres and classes will be equipped with trained educators, appropriate facilities and quality services, with due consideration given to the needs of families requiring assistance.
“Children are the future of the country, and every child deserves the opportunity to learn, grow and reach their full potential,” he told Bernama recently.
Kindergarten operator Lim Suh Yin, 42, who has three children with special needs, also welcomed plans for dedicated centres for autistic children, noting they require specialised knowledge, skills and tailored teaching methods.
She said teachers must understand that each autistic child has distinct characteristics, behaviours and needs to ensure their learning and development are adequately supported.
“Caring for and understanding these children requires specific skills, as each child has different characteristics and needs and responds to different approaches.
“Those without specialised training may struggle to understand autistic children’s behaviour and identify suitable learning methods for them,” she said, stressing the importance of dedicated centres or classes with trained educators and professional support to promote the development of autistic children.
Mulya Aina Mohamad, 43, whose 12-year-old child is autistic, said plans to open more specialised classes would give parents hope, especially those from low-income households who face financial barriers to accessing private education services.
She said suitable early childhood education would enable autistic children to participate in learning activities, receive training and access support suited to their needs before starting school.
“Not all families can afford private education, while rural parents struggle to find suitable education and guidance for children under seven,” she said, adding that more specialised classes would help parents and raise awareness of autistic children’s needs and available support.
Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced in Budget 2027 that two Permata Kurnia centres would be built in Pahang and Melaka to provide education, support and training for autistic children, while more than 130 new Tabika Tunas Istimewa classes would open in rural areas nationwide to improve access to early support for autistic children from low-income families. — Bernama

Title: Nepal turns to SMART’s drones, detection gear after declining two Malaysian rescue offers
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 26 — Malaysia’s third offer to assist Nepal in its search and rescue (SAR) operations for mud flood victims was accepted after two earlier offers were turned down, paving the way for the deployment of the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART), equipped with technical expertise and advanced detection equipment.
SMART commander Senior Fire Superintendent 1 Abdul Manaf Che Isa, who led the mission, said Malaysia initially offered to send 50 rescuers, followed by a second offer of 25 personnel with SAR equipment, but Nepal declined both offers because it already had sufficient rescue teams.
He said Nepal’s government eventually accepted Malaysia’s third offer, which involved deploying just 11 SMART personnel, nine high-capacity drones and specialised detection equipment, after several rounds of discussions.
“Our initial offer was to deploy 50 personnel for SAR operations, but Nepal had already deployed its own rescue teams and declined the offer. The Nepalese government needed specialised equipment and expertise that it lacked.
“At the same time, we did not want to travel there only to find that there was no work for us to do,” he said in a recent interview with Bernama on SMART’s humanitarian mission in Nepal.
According to Abdul Manaf, Nepal declined the first two offers not because it did not need Malaysia’s assistance, but because it had already mobilised enough rescuers, including members of the military, police and fire services, volunteers, and international SAR teams from countries including China and South Korea.
He said SMART’s strengths included high-capacity drones for aerial surveys, mapping disaster-hit areas and locating victims, as well as specialised equipment capable of detecting sounds and movement beneath mud deposits.
“Buildings may be buried beneath mud while their structures remain intact. The area may look clear from above, but this equipment enables us to detect sounds and movement. Such equipment was not available there, and the authorities saw the need for it,” he said.
Abdul Manaf said diplomatic engagement through the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu also played a key role in convincing the Nepalese military that SMART could provide the technical assistance needed, including SAR detection equipment, search cameras, satellite phones and specialised communication systems.
He said the Nepalese government prioritised self-sufficient international relief teams, a criterion that aligned with SMART’s capabilities recognised by the International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG), as disaster victims need local shelter, food supplies and logistical support.
Once Nepal’s government had approved the mission, the SMART team was deployed to the Nepalese military’s tactical base in Trishuli, from where it took a helicopter to reach search areas no longer accessible by road because of infrastructure damage.
Abdul Manaf said the mud floods had drastically altered the terrain, making existing maps unreliable and forcing SMART personnel to use drones, GPS, and physical observations to determine search routes.
“For ground operations, we could not rely fully on maps as the terrain had changed significantly from what they depicted. Roads and buildings had been destroyed, leaving only rocks, sand and mud,” he said, noting that mud deposits reached depths of three to five metres, and up to eight metres in some areas.
He said heavy rain and overcast conditions also hampered helicopter operations, forcing personnel to be dropped off on hillsides before walking for more than an hour to reach the operation site, while also facing the risk of further disasters.
He said SMART personnel spent three days conducting secondary searches with Nepalese military tactical teams in designated sectors between Timure and Syabrubesi, using their expertise and specialised equipment to search the last known location of the Malaysians reported missing, but found no survivors.
SMART also shared aerial images and drone footage with the families concerned and handed over equipment and supplies to the Nepalese military to support continued search operations.
Abdul Manaf stressed that the SMART team had searched as extensively as possible amid difficult geographical, weather and safety conditions, adding that SAR operations focused first on rescuing survivors, with recovery efforts undertaken if necessary.
He also appealed to the families to remain resilient and patient while awaiting further steps by the Malaysian and Nepalese governments through coordination by the Foreign Ministry. — Bernama

Title: Abang Johari confirms AI data centre plan in Sarawak under US$50b investment
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 26 — The US$50 billion investment announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim recently includes strategic plans by a major international company to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) data centre in Tanjung Embang.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said further details, including the name of the company involved, could not be disclosed at this stage to preserve the confidentiality of the corporate transaction.
“What the Prime Minister said is true, but it is still at the planning stage. There is indeed a proposal to invest in an artificial intelligence data centre.
“We cannot disclose the amount for now because it involves a top international company... We cannot reveal its name, but it is indeed there,” he told reporters after officiating at the Sarawak Urban Forum (SUF) 2.0 here today.
Earlier in his speech, Abang Johari revealed that the Prime Minister himself had contacted him to enquire about the entry of the world’s leading technology investor into Sarawak.
The Premier said the international technology giant had chosen Kuching as its investment destination because it viewed Sarawak as a forward-looking state that was aggressively transitioning towards a new economy.
“The topmost technology company in the world is coming to Kuching. Why? Because they see that we are forward-looking.
“Sarawak is transitioning to a new economy and we have prepared Sarawakians in terms of human capital. We provide free education, and that is why they like it because they know they will have good people to work with them,” he said.
On Saturday, the media reported that the Prime Minister had revealed that a global technology company had chosen Malaysia, including Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, for a US$50 billion investment in the AI sector. — Bernama

Title: Live pig imports from Sarawak to Selangor subject to strict controls since July 2025, says deputy minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The import of live pigs from Sarawak to Selangor since July 2025 has been carried out with import licence approval and is subject to compliance with strict control procedures to help stabilise market supply and prices following disruptions to the pig farming industry caused by the spread of African Swine Fever (ASF).
Agriculture and Food Security Deputy Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin said the policy had been repeatedly communicated to the media and the Dewan Rakyat, and should therefore not be portrayed as a new measure introduced only this year.
“I deeply regret that allegations and accusations have been made without examining the facts, with some even attempting to link the issue to the Sultan of Selangor’s royal decree and turn it into a controversy based on inaccurate information,” he said in a statement today.
He said Sarawak Minister of Food Industry, Commodity and Regional Development Datuk Seri Dr Stephen Rundi Utom had announced the matter in July 2025 during an official loading ceremony at Pending Port, Sarawak.
Further clarification had also been provided by Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup, who was then Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister, and by Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu through oral question sessions and written replies in the Dewan Rakyat.
Chan said Selangor Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim had also explained that the state government allowed the issuance of import licences for live pigs from Sarawak, subject to strict conditions and control procedures. The animals are not permitted to stop at any other location and have to be transported directly to a slaughterhouse in Rawang.
“I was also informed that strict standard operating procedures (SOPs) have been established from the outset to ensure that the handling of livestock at Port Klang is conducted in a controlled and orderly manner.
“Among the measures imposed is the restriction of live animal unloading activities to between 8 pm and 5 am. The animals are unloaded using specialised cages before being transferred directly onto lorries for delivery to the slaughterhouse in Rawang,” he said.
He said the procedures are to ensure smooth livestock transportation, minimise handling time at the port and reduce the risk of contamination and disruption to the surrounding environment.
Therefore, he said, claims that the operation had affected cleanliness and sanitation at the port should not be made without examining the SOPs and control measures in place, stressing that such allegations must be supported by facts and credible evidence.
Chan said he had conducted a working visit to a modern pig farm in Simunjan, Sarawak, in April to observe its operations and procedures for exporting live pigs to Singapore and Selangor.
“During the visit, I had the opportunity to observe the implementation of stringent biosecurity measures, including the use of livestock transport vessels that meet the stipulated specifications.
“These measures are important to ensure that livestock transportation is carried out in a controlled and orderly manner, taking into account animal health and risk management throughout the delivery chain,” he said, adding that the issue should be discussed professionally and based on facts, rather than assumptions or inaccurate information.
He also hoped that all parties would refer to valid information and refrain from making statements that could cause confusion or unwarranted public concern. — Bernama

Title: Court of Appeal slashes Klang council’s RM117m dumpsite damages bill to RM3m
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 26 — The Court of Appeal today reduced the damages payable by the Klang Municipal Council, now known as the Klang Royal City Council, to property developer NBC Land Sdn Bhd from RM117 million to RM3 million in a dispute over the rehabilitation of a former dumpsite.
A three-man bench comprising Datuk Ismail Brahim, K. Muniandy and Datuk Dean Wayne Daly also set aside nearly RM50 million in pre-judgment interest previously imposed by the Shah Alam High Court on the local authority.
Delivering the broad grounds of judgment, Justice Muniandy said the Shah Alam High Court was plainly wrong in principle and in law in the assessment of damages which warranted the intervention of the appellate court.
“The contractual damages flowing from the breach of the Dec 2, 2003 agreement must be assessed based on the works contemplated under the contract, namely the soil capping scheme estimated at RM6 million of which the appellant (Klang Municipal Council) was to bear 50 percent,” he said.
Justice Muniandy said the agreement reached by parties was not an open warranty by the local authority to eradicate all waste or convert the dumpsite into virgin ground, rather the consensus was based on a specific proposal by the company’s own consultant to execute an in-situ soil capping of approximately 1.5 meters of compacted soil over the waste, at an estimated cost of RM6 million.
“The parties agreed to share this estimated cost of RM6 million equally, 50 percent each (RM3 million each),” he said.
Justice Muniandy said that the High Court also erred in law in awarding the pre-judgment interest under Section 11 of the Civil Law Act 1956 as the award of pre-judgment interest cannot stand because the rehabilitation works were never executed and the landfill was also never excavated and third-party contractors were also not paid.
“To award nearly nine years of pre-judgment interest, amounting to approximately RM50 million, on an unspent, unliquidated estimate of works penalises the appellant (Klang Municipal Council) and produces an impermissible windfall,” he said.
Therefore, he said the court substitute the High Court’s award with RM3 million in damages, representing the council’s agreed 50 per cent share of the RM6 million rehabilitation cost.
NBC Land acquired the land and obtained approval for residential development. It is not disputed that NBC Land knew at the time of acquisition that the land had been used as a dumpsite.
On Dec 2, 2003, following discussions between parties, an agreement was reached whereby the council agreed to carry out rehabilitation works in respect of the subject land and to bear 50 percent of the rehabilitation cost which was estimated at RM6 million. However, the council did not carry out the rehabilitation works.
In July 2020, the earlier panel of the Court of Appeal had held that the council was in breach of the agreement and remitted the matter back to the High Court for assessment of damages. The High Court proceeded to assess damages and in Feb this year entered judgment in favour of the company for RM117 million.
At the proceeding today, Tan Sri Tommy Thomas, Datuk Seri Nik Suhaimi Nik Sulaiman, Muhd Fadzli Amin Muhd Yusoff and Atiqah Azman represented the Klang Municipal Council while Harold Tan Kok Leng represented NBC Land. — Bernama

Title: Zahid extends aid to two Bernama, NST journalists injured in Ipoh-Lumut road crash
Article:
IPOH, Oct 26 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has extended financial assistance and words of encouragement to two journalists from the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) and the New Straits Times (NST) who were injured in a road accident on the Ipoh-Lumut road yesterday.
The contributions were delivered today by his press secretary, Shuhaimi Mohamed, to Bernama journalist Nur Afiradina Arshad, 34, and NST journalist Zahratulhayat Mat Arif, 37, at their homes in Semenyih and Ipoh, respectively.
Speaking at Zahratulhayat’s residence in Klebang Harmoni, Shuhaimi said Ahmad Zahid had also pledged to monitor their recovery and provide further assistance where needed.
“We hope Dina and Zahra will recover quickly and be able to return to work. Their contributions extend beyond Bagan Datuk to the whole of Perak,” he said.
Several Perak-based media practitioners were also present.
Shuhaimi said Ahmad Zahid appreciated the solidarity and moral support shown by the Ipoh media fraternity towards the injured journalists.
He added that the deputy prime minister, who also chairs the Road Safety Committee, regularly reminded motorists to remain vigilant, particularly on poorly lit roads, and to prioritise their safety.
The two journalists were travelling from Ipoh to Bagan Datuk to cover an event scheduled to be attended by Ahmad Zahid when their Perodua Bezza was reportedly struck by a lorry in Menglembu.
Nur Afiradina was taken for treatment in the yellow zone of Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital as she sustained a neck injury, abrasions on her body, and a sprained ankle, while Zahratulhayat received outpatient treatment for minor injuries at the same hospital. — Bernama

Title: Dewan Rakyat Speaker asks Rayer to write formally over Takiyuddin’s ‘munafik’ remark
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Jelutong Member of Parliament RSN Rayer has been asked to write an official letter to Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul if he wants Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu) to be referred to the Parliament Rights and Privileges Committee.
Johari said that the committee will examine the matter regarding Takiyuddin’s use of the word “hypocrite” (munafik), which was linked to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the debate on the 2027 Budget last Monday, before making any decision.
“I will summon the committee to review it, and it will not be my decision afterwards. The decision will be made by the committee, which consists of members from both sides [of the house], and I will only announce it,” he said during the policy-level winding-up session of the Supply Bill 2027 (2027 Budget) debate in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Earlier, Rayer raised the issue under Standing Order 36(4), which prohibits members of the House from using unparliamentary language.
Johari explained that he had previously asked Takiyuddin to retract the word, but the PAS Secretary-General, via a letter dated October 22, suggested that a mediation process be held without retracting the word.
Johari also expressed disappointment when Takiyuddin subsequently made a statement to the media regarding the letter before he had the opportunity to respond.
Rayer stated that he complies with the rules of the House and believes Takiyuddin should do the same.
Last Wednesday, Johari said he had examined the Hansard before ruling that Takiyuddin must retract the word, either in the Dewan Rakyat or through a written explanation to the Speaker. — Bernama

Title: Melaka schools to remain open amid haze, outdoor activities suspended if API exceeds 100
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 26 — All educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Melaka will operate as usual tomorrow, said the Melaka State Education Department.
In a statement, the Melaka Education Department announced that outdoor classroom activities may proceed as usual in areas recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading below 100.
However, the department stated that all outdoor activities, including physical education, co-curricular and sports activities, camps, celebrations, assemblies, and activities in open halls, must be suspended if the API reading exceeds 100, in line with MOE Circular No. 1 of 2019.
“The End-of-Session Academic Assessment (UASA) will continue according to the schedule set by each school, including internal examinations.
“Schools are also urged to exercise due consideration for students unable to attend for health reasons, including permitting them to sit for the examinations at a later date,” the statement read.
The department also advised students to wear face masks, particularly those experiencing respiratory symptoms or belonging to high-risk groups.
“Parents and guardians concerned about the effects of the haze on their children’s health may choose not to send them to school, provided they inform the school.
“Parents, guardians, and all members of the education community are advised to refer to the Melaka Education Department’s official channels for the latest information on the operation of educational institutions,” the statement read.
Meanwhile, the Pahang Education Department announced in a statement that all schools in the state will operate as usual starting tomorrow, with any changes to be communicated from time to time through the respective District Education Offices. — Bernama

Title: Fuziah: PKR fields seven new faces among nine candidates for Melaka polls
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 26 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) is fielding seven new faces among its nine candidates in the upcoming Melaka state election, reflecting its push for leadership renewal.
Its secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the new faces make up 77.8 per cent of the party’s line-up, including four young candidates.
She said three women are also among the candidates, accounting for 33.3 per cent of the party’s total.
“Since the announcement of the candidates, I have visited eight state constituency election operations centres to assess preparations, meet campaign workers and help coordinate campaign machinery.
“These visits will continue until tomorrow to ensure preparations at the constituency level are progressing smoothly,” she said in a social media post today.
Fuziah said political renewal was not merely about introducing new faces but also about creating opportunities for the younger generation and women to take on greater leadership roles and represent the aspirations of the people.
On Saturday, Prime Minister and Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that the coalition would contest 21 seats in the Melaka state election next month.
Of the total, PKR will contest nine seats, while DAP will field candidates in seven and Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) in five.
The new faces fielded by PKR are Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri in Tanjung Bidara, Mohd Khuzairie Mohd Kamal Kannan (Rembia), Denesh Palasubraniam (Asahan), Datuk Azman Abidin (Paya Rumput), Muhammad Hakimin Mokhtar (Ayer Molek), Esma Eazreen Husin (Rim) and Muhammad Faiq Azman (Serkam).
The other two women candidates are former Machap Jaya assemblywoman Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin, who is contesting the same seat, and Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir (Kelebang). — Bernama

Title: British nationals top KLIA drug mule arrests, drugs worth RM202.76m seized
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — A total of 77 cases linked to drug mule syndicates at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) were recorded between January and Oct 15, with 93 individuals arrested.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said these cases involved the seizure of 2,526.28 kilogrammes (kg) of drugs, with an estimated value of RM202.76 million.
He said the seized substances comprised 2,407.27 kg of cannabis (64 cases), 77.837 kg of methamphetamine (four cases), 22.11 kg of ketamine (four cases), 15.585 kg of cocaine (three cases), and 3.475 kg of a mixture of ketamine and cannabis (two cases).
“Out of the total 93 arrests, nationals from the United Kingdom accounted for the highest number at 26, followed by Malaysia (23), Singapore (11), Japan (five), and France (six).
“Meanwhile, there were two individuals each from Hong Kong, Indonesia, India, Ireland, Portugal, and Germany and one individual each from the Netherlands, Greece, Sweden, Slovakia, the United States, Brazil, Uganda, Zambia, Thailand, and China,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
Regarding the breakdown of the 77 cases, he said 45 cases were recorded through the cooperation of enforcement agencies comprising 41 cases handled by Aviation Security (AVSEC) Auxiliary Police of Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) at KLIA, and four cases by the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS).
“Another 25 cases involved actions by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID), including the KLIA Narcotics Crime Investigation Division and the Selangor contingent police headquarters (IPK).
“Additionally, seven cases were recorded through follow-up operations, which led to the arrest of 12 individuals and the seizure of 571.59 kilogrammes of cannabis flowers,” he said.
Hussein noted that these successes reflect the ongoing commitment of the department, in collaboration with relevant enforcement agencies, to combat drug smuggling and curb syndicates that exploit individuals as drug mules.
“The public is also reminded not to be easily deceived by suspicious job offers or promises of lucrative rewards especially those involving the transport of luggage or items belonging to others to foreign countries.
“Furthermore, the public is urged to refrain from carrying items belonging to other people abroad without knowing their contents, and to report any suspicious activities to the police,” he said. — Bernama
